results.answer:
# Key Assumptions for Adverse Event Data Collection and Coding

Based on the SDTMIG v3.4 knowledge base, the following are the key assumptions for adverse event data collection and coding:

## 1. Scope and Definition of Adverse Events

The AE dataset includes clinical data describing "any untoward medical occurrence in a patient or clinical investigation subject administered a pharmaceutical product and which does not necessarily have to have a causal relationship with this treatment" (ICH E2A). Sponsors may extend or limit the scope of AE collection in consultation with regulatory authorities (e.g., collecting pre-treatment events related to trial conduct, not collecting events assessed as efficacy endpoints). The events included should be consistent with protocol requirements. **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_1]**

## 2. AE Description and Coding

- **AETERM** is the **topic variable** capturing the verbatim term collected for the event. It is a **required variable** and must have a value. **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_2a]**
- **AEMODIFY** is a **permissible variable** included if the sponsor's procedure permits modification of a verbatim term for coding. **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_2b]**
- **AEDECOD** is the **preferred term** derived from the coding dictionary (e.g., MedDRA). It is a **required variable** and must have a value. The dictionary name and version must be provided in Define-XML. **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_2c]**
- **AEBODSYS** is the **system organ class (SOC)** from the coding dictionary. This value may differ from the primary SOC in the dictionary's standard hierarchy. It is expected to be populated. **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_2d]**

## 3. Prespecified Terms and Presence/Absence of Events

- Adverse events may be collected via **free text** or a **prespecified list of terms**. **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_4a]**
- **AEPRESP** = "Y" indicates the event was prespecified on the CRF. **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_4a]**
- If it is important to know which prespecified AEs were **not reported**, these data should be submitted in a **Findings class dataset** (e.g., FA — Findings About Events or Interventions). **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_4b]**
- For studies collecting both prespecified and free-text events: AEPRESP = "Y" for prespecified events, **null** for free-text events. AEPRESP may be omitted if all events are free text. **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_4c]**
- **Do not include records** for subjects with "no adverse events" — only include records for events that actually occurred. **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_4d]**

## 4. Seriousness Classification

- If "Serious?" is answered "No", seriousness category variables (e.g., AESCAN, AESCONG) may be **null**. If "Yes", at least one category variable will have "Y". **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_7a]**
- If the CRF collects a response for each seriousness category, all category variables (e.g., AESDTH, AESHOSP) would be populated and AESER derived. **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_7a]**
- Categories "Involves cancer" (AESCAN) and "Occurred with overdose" (AESOD) are **not part of the ICH definition** but are available for studies under pre-ICH guidelines. **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_7b]**
- Descriptions of "Other Medically Important SAE" should be placed in **SUPPAE** using QNAM = **AEOSOSP**. **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_7c]**

## 5. Severity vs. Toxicity Grade

- For studies using a standard toxicity scale (e.g., CTCAE v3.0), use **AETOXGR** instead of **AESEV**. In most cases, only one is populated. The dictionary name and version must be in Define-XML. **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_7d]**

## 6. Record Structure (One Record per Event)

The AE domain structure is **1 record per adverse event per subject**. The sponsor defines what constitutes an event. Options include:

- **One record per event** covering start to finish (summary record "collapsed" to highest severity, causality, seriousness, and final outcome).
- **One record per event** with changes over time submitted as separate events, or alternatively in a **Findings About Events and Interventions** dataset (FA). **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_7e]**

## 7. Use of EPOCH and TAETORD

- **EPOCH** in the AE domain should be based on **AESTDTC** (start of the adverse event), not AEENDTC. The computational method in Define-XML should describe assumptions for ambiguous cases (e.g., same-day epoch transitions). **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_8]**
- Similarly, **TAETORD** should be based on the start of the adverse event. **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md — item_8]**

## 8. Relationship to Other Domains

- When disposition (DS) is related to an AE (e.g., death due to heart failure), the relationship is represented in **RELREC** using IDVAR = DSSEQ and AESEQ with a common RELID. **[Source: domains/DS/examples.md — Example 4]**
- Prespecified AE occurrence data can be represented in **FA** (Findings About Events or Interventions) with FAOBJ = AEDECOD value, and corresponding AE records with AEPRESP = "Y". **[Source: domains/FA/examples.md — Example 4]**
- Severity assessments over time (snapshots/slices of an AE) can be represented in **FA** using FATESTCD = "SEV" with FAOBJ = AEDECOD. **[Source: domains/FA/examples.md — Example 6]**

## 9. Supplemental Qualifiers

- Non-standard variables (e.g., "Other Medically Important SAE" description) are placed in **SUPPAE** using QNAM codes (e.g., AEOSP) linked via IDVAR = AESEQ and IDVARVAL. **[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/examples.md — Example 1]**

## 10. Clinical Events (CE) Domain

- Collection of write-in events on a CE CRF should be done with caution — sponsors must ensure all adverse events are recorded in the **AE domain**. **[Source: domains/CE/assumptions.md — item_3]**

results.answer:
## TV (Trial Visits) Domain — Purpose and Variables

### Purpose

The TV (Trial Visits) domain is a **Trial Design** domain that describes the **protocol-defined planned schedule of subject encounters** at the healthcare facility where the study is being conducted. It defines the planned visits for the trial, including their timing rules and relationships to trial elements and epochs.

Key purposes include:
- Defining the planned clinical encounters (visits) as described in the protocol
- Providing visit timing rules (start and end rules) relative to elements or epochs
- Serving as the reference against which actual subject visits (in the SV domain) can be compared
- Supporting identification of planned but not completed visits **[Source: domains/TV/assumptions.md — overview]**

The TV dataset, together with the TD (Trial Disease Assessments) dataset, provides the **planned scheduling of assessments** to which a subject's actual visits and disease assessments can be compared. **[Source: domains/TV/assumptions.md — overview]**

---

### Variables

The TV domain contains the following variables (from the specification):

| Order | Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core | Controlled Terms |
|-------|----------|-------|------|------|------|-----------------|
| 1 | STUDYID | Study Identifier | Char | Identifier | Req | — |
| 2 | DOMAIN | Domain Abbreviation | Char | Identifier | Req | TV |
| 3 | VISITNUM | Visit Number | Num | Topic | Req | — |
| 4 | VISIT | Visit Name | Char | Synonym Qualifier | Req | — |
| 5 | VISITDY | Planned Study Day of Visit | Num | Timing | Perm | — |
| 6 | ARMCD | Planned Arm Code | Char | Topic | Perm | (Arm Code codelist) |
| 7 | ARM | Planned Arm | Char | Synonym Qualifier | Perm | — |
| 8 | TVSTRL | Visit Start Rule | Char | Rule | Req | — |
| 9 | TVENRL | Visit End Rule | Char | Rule | Perm | — |

**[Source: domains/TV/spec.md — VISIT, TVSTRL; domains/TV/examples.md — Example 1]**

---

### Key Variable Details

- **VISITNUM** (Req, Topic): Numeric visit number used for sorting; values should match the planned chronological order of visits. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — §4.4.5]**
- **VISIT** (Req, Synonym Qualifier): Description of the clinical encounter, often defined in the protocol. Used in addition to VISITNUM as a text description. **[Source: domains/TV/spec.md — VISIT]**
- **VISITDY** (Perm, Timing): The planned study day of the start of the visit (not the actual study day). **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — §4.4.5]**
- **TVSTRL** (Req, Rule): Rule describing when the visit starts, in relation to the sequence of elements. **[Source: domains/TV/spec.md — TVSTRL]**
- **TVENRL** (Perm, Rule): Rule describing when the visit ends. **[Source: domains/TV/examples.md — Example 1]**
- **ARMCD/ARM** (Perm): Populated only when the visit schedule differs by arm; left blank when the schedule is the same for all arms. **[Source: domains/TV/assumptions.md — item_1]**

---

### Related Domains

- **Same class (Trial Design):** TA, TD, TE, TI, TM, TS
- **Trial Design:** TA — visits reference arms
- **Trial Design:** SE — planned visits vs actual subject elements

**[Source: domains/TV/spec.md — Related Domains]**

---

### Data Structure

The general structure is **"One Record per Planned Visit per Arm"** — though for many blinded trials where the schedule is the same for all arms, the structure simplifies to **"One Record per Planned Visit"** (with ARMCD left blank). **[Source: domains/TV/assumptions.md — item_1]**

## LBTESTCD — Lab Test or Examination Short Name

Based on the retrieved context, here is the complete specification for the LBTESTCD variable in the LB domain:

### Variable Definition

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Label** | Lab Test or Examination Short Name |
| **Type** | Char |
| **Role** | Topic |
| **Core** | Required |
| **Controlled Terms** | C65047 (Laboratory Test Code) |

**[Source: domains/LB/spec.md — LBTESTCD]**

### Naming Constraints

The CDISC Notes specify three constraints on LBTESTCD values:

1. **Maximum length**: Cannot be longer than 8 characters.
2. **First character**: Cannot start with a number (e.g., "1TEST" is not valid).
3. **Permitted characters**: Cannot contain characters other than letters, numbers, or underscores.

**Examples provided**: "ALT", "LDH"

**[Source: domains/LB/spec.md — LBTESTCD]**

### Role Description

As a **Topic variable**, LBTESTCD specifies the focus of the observation — in this case, the short name of the laboratory measurement or test. It can be used as a column name when converting a dataset from a vertical to a horizontal format.

**[Source: chapters/ch02_fundamentals.md — §2.1 Observations and Variables]**

### Controlled Terminology

LBTESTCD uses the **Laboratory Test Code** codelist (C65047). The full list of permitted values is maintained in the terminology file at `terminology/core/lb_part2.md`. This codelist contains hundreds of standard short names for laboratory tests (e.g., "ALT", "LDH", "KIM1S", "KL6", "LACTICAC", etc.).

**[Source: domains/LB/spec.md — Controlled Terminology section, referencing C65047 → terminology/core/lb_part2.md]**

### Relationship to LBTEST

LBTESTCD is the short name counterpart to **LBTEST** (Lab Test or Examination Name, C67154), which serves as a Synonym Qualifier. LBTEST contains the full verbatim test name (e.g., "Alanine Aminotransferase" for LBTESTCD="ALT") and cannot exceed 40 characters.

**[Source: domains/LB/spec.md — LBTEST]**

### Summary

LBTESTCD is a **Required** Topic variable that provides a standardized, abbreviated identifier for laboratory tests, constrained to 8 alphanumeric/underscore characters, drawn from the CDISC Laboratory Test Code codelist (C65047).

results.answer:
## EX (Exposure) Domain — Purpose and Topic Variable

### Domain Purpose

The EX (Exposure) domain represents **protocol-specified study treatment administrations** that have been received by a subject. It is an **Interventions** class domain. Key characteristics:

- **Scope**: Represents treatments that are protocol-specified (e.g., investigational product, placebo, active comparator). Non-protocol-specified treatments go in CM (Concomitant/Prior Medications) or another Interventions domain. **[Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md — item_1a]**
- **Derived dataset**: EX is recognized in most cases as a **derived dataset**, where EXDOSU reflects the protocol-specified unit. Collected data points (e.g., number of tablets, total volume infused) are represented in the EC (Exposure as Collected) domain. **[Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md — item_1b, item_5]**
- **Required**: The EX domain is required for all studies that include protocol-specified study treatment. **[Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md — item_1c]**
- **Record structure**: Contains 1 record per constant-dosing interval per subject. A constant-dosing interval is any period described in terms of a known treatment given at a consistent dose, frequency, infusion rate, etc. **[Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md — item_1d]**
- **Relationship to EC**: When both EC and EX are implemented, the relationship between records can be described using RELREC. **[Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md — item_5]**

### Topic Variable: EXTRT

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Label** | Name of Treatment |
| **Type** | Char |
| **Role** | Topic |
| **Core** | Required (Req) |
| **Controlled Terms** | — (not specified; sponsor-defined) |

**[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md — EX — Exposure (Interventions)]**

**CDISC Notes / Rules**:
- EXTRT captures the name of the protocol-specified study treatment and is the **topic variable**. It is a **required variable** and must have a value. **[Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md — item_2a]**
- EXTRT must include **only the treatment name** and must **not** include dosage, formulation, or other qualifying information. For example, "ASPIRIN 100MG TABLET" is not valid; this should be expressed as EXTRT = "ASPIRIN", EXDOSE = "100", EXDOSU = "mg", and EXDOSFRM = "TABLET". **[Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md — item_2a]**
- Doses of placebo should be represented by EXTRT = "PLACEBO" and EXDOSE = "0". **[Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md — item_2b]**

### Related Domains

- **Same class (Interventions)**: AG, CM, EC, ML, PR, SU **[Source: domains/EX/spec.md — Related Domains]**
- **Shared Dataset**: EC (Exposure as Collected) — for collected exposure data points that are used to derive EX records **[Source: domains/EX/spec.md — Related Domains]**

Based on the retrieved context, here is the role of MHTERM and the assumptions guiding medical history data collection in the MH domain.

### Role of MHTERM

- **Label:** Reported Term for the Medical History
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Topic
- **Core:** Req
- **Controlled Terms:** (none)
- **CDISC Notes:** Verbatim or preprinted CRF term for the medical condition or event.

**[Source: domains/MH/spec.md]**

### Assumptions Guiding Medical History Data Collection

1.  **MH Description and Coding:**
    - **MHTERM** is the Topic variable and captures the verbatim or prespecified term for the condition or event. It is required and must have a value.
    - **MHMODIFY** is a permissible variable for sponsor-modified terms prior to coding.
    - If a standard dictionary is used for coding, **MHDECOD** is populated with the preferred term, and the dictionary name/version is documented in Define-XML.
    - **MHBODSYS** is the System Organ Class (SOC) from the coding dictionary.
    - If a CRF collects medical history by prespecified body systems and the sponsor also codes terms, **MHDECOD** and **MHBODSYS** come from the dictionary, while **MHCAT** and **MHSCAT** are used for the prespecified CRF body systems.

    **[Source: domains/MH/assumptions.md — item_2]**

2.  **Additional Categorization and Grouping:**
    - **MHCAT** and **MHSCAT** may be populated with the sponsor's predefined categorization (often from the CRF). This should not be a generic group like "Medical History" (redundant with the domain code). Examples include "General Medical History" or "Allergy Medical History".
    - **MHGRPID** is used to link related records at the subject level within the MH domain (e.g., grouping records for a single disease), not as a substitute for MHCAT/MHSCAT.

    **[Source: domains/MH/assumptions.md — item_3]**

3.  **Prespecified Terms and Occurrence:**
    - Medical history is collected either as free text or from a prespecified list of terms.
    - **MHPRESP** and **MHOCCUR** are used together to indicate if a term was prespecified and whether it occurred.
    - **MHPRESP = "Y"** indicates the term was prespecified.
    - **MHOCCUR = "Y"** indicates the event occurred; **"N"** indicates it did not.
    - For free-text reports, both MHPRESP and MHOCCUR should be null.
    - **MHSTAT** and **MHREASND** provide information about prespecified questions for which no response was collected (e.g., MHSTAT = "NOT DONE").

    | Situation | MHPRESP | MHOCCUR | MHSTAT |
    |-----------|---------|---------|--------|
    | Spontaneously reported event occurred | (null) | (null) | (null) |
    | Pre-specified event occurred | Y | Y | (null) |
    | Pre-specified event did not occur | Y | N | (null) |
    | Pre-specified event has no response | Y | (null) | NOT DONE |

    **[Source: domains/MH/assumptions.md — item_4]**

4.  **Timing Variables:**
    - **MHDTC** is the Date/Time of History Collection (ISO 8601 format).
    - **MHSTDTC** and **MHENDTC** are the start and end date/times of the medical history event.
    - **MHENRF** (End Relative to Reference Period) and **MHENRTPT** (End Relative to Reference Time Point) are used to indicate whether the event was ongoing or had ended relative to a reference point (e.g., "DURING/AFTER" for ongoing, "BEFORE" for ended). Controlled terms for these variables come from codelist C66728.

    **[Source: domains/MH/spec.md; domains/MH/examples.md — Example 1, Example 2]**

**[Source: domains/EG/spec.md — variable table; Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md — EG section]**

---

## EGTESTCD Variable Definition

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Order** | 10 |
| **Label** | ECG Test or Examination Short Name |
| **Type** | Char |
| **Controlled Terms** | C71153; C120523 |
| **Role** | Topic |
| **Core** | Req |
| **CDISC Notes** | Short name of the measurement, test, or examination described in EGTEST. Cannot exceed 8 characters, cannot start with a number, and cannot contain characters other than letters, numbers, or underscores. Examples: "PRAG", "QRSAG". Test codes are in 2 separate codelists: one for tests based on regular 10-second ECGs (EGTESTCD) and one for tests based on Holter monitoring (HETESTCD). |

**[Source: domains/EG/spec.md — EGTESTCD entry]**

---

## Controlled Terminology Codelists for EGTESTCD

EGTESTCD references **two separate codelists**:

### 1. ECG Test Code (C71153) — Regular 10-second ECGs
- **Extensible:** Yes
- **Purpose:** Contains test codes for standard 10-second ECG measurements (e.g., heart rate, intervals, axes)
- **Used for:** Standard clinic/office ECGs

### 2. Holter ECG Test Code (C120523) — Holter Monitoring
- **Extensible:** Yes
- **Purpose:** Contains test codes for Holter/continuous ECG monitoring assessments
- **Example values** (from terminology file):
  - `AVCOND` — Atrioventricular Conduction
  - `AXISVOLT` — Axis and Voltage
  - `CHYPTENL` — Chamber Hypertrophy or Enlargement
  - `EGCOMP` — Comparison to a Prior ECG
  - `INTP` — Interpretation
  - `IVTIACD` — Intraventricular-Intraatrial Conduction
  - `MI` — Myocardial Infarction
  - `PACEMAKR` — Pacemaker
  - `RHYNOS` — Rhythm Not Otherwise Specified
  - `SNRARRY` — Sinus Node Rhythms and Arrhythmias
  - `SPRARRY` — Supraventricular Arrhythmias
  - `SPRTARRY` — Supraventricular Tachyarrhythmias
  - `STSTWUW` — ST Segment, T wave, and U wave
  - `TECHQUAL` — Technical Quality
  - `VTARRY` — Ventricular Arrhythmias
  - `VTTARRY` — Ventricular Tachyarrhythmias

**[Source: domains/EG/spec.md — Controlled Terminology section; Source: terminology/core/eg_part3.md — Holter ECG Test Code (C120523)]**

---

## Key Business Rules

1. **Two separate codelists** exist for tests based on regular 10-second ECGs (C71153) and Holter monitoring (C120523). The same separation applies to EGTEST (C71152 vs C120524) and EGSTRESC (C71150 vs C120522/C101834). **[Source: domains/EG/assumptions.md — item_2]**

2. **EGCAT** is used to categorize observations (e.g., "MEASUREMENT", "FINDING", "INTERVAL") and has no controlled terminology. **[Source: domains/EG/spec.md — EGCAT entry]**

3. **EGMETHOD** uses the ECG Test Method codelist (C71151), which includes values such as "12 LEAD STANDARD", "12 LEAD MASON LIKAR", "HOLTER CONTINUOUS ECG RECORDING", etc. **[Source: domains/EG/spec.md — EGMETHOD entry; Source: terminology/core/eg_part2.md — ECG Test Method (C71151)]**

4. **EGLNKID** can be used to link EG records to procedures in the PR domain (e.g., a 24-hour Holter monitor procedure). **[Source: domains/PR/examples.md — Example 2]**

5. **EGDRVFL** (Derived Flag) uses the No Yes Response codelist (C66742) to indicate derived results (e.g., QTcB and QTcF intervals). **[Source: domains/EG/examples.md — Example 1, rows 5-6]**

results.answer:
## SUPPQUAL Definition and Purpose

**SUPPQUAL** (Supplemental Qualifiers for [domain name]) is a **Relationship** class dataset model used to capture non-standard variables (NSVs) that cannot be accommodated in the standard SDTM domain datasets. **[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md §6.2]**

The SDTM does not allow the addition of new variables to standard domains. Therefore, the Supplemental Qualifiers special-purpose dataset model is used to capture sponsor-defined variables and their association to parent records in general-observation class datasets (Events, Findings, Interventions), Demographics (DM), and Subject Visits (SV). **[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md]**

### Key Variables

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core |
|----------|-------|------|------|------|
| QNAM | Qualifier Variable Name | Char | Topic | Req |
| QLABEL | Qualifier Variable Label | Char | Synonym Qualifier | Req |
| QVAL | Data Value | Char | Result Qualifier | Req |
| QORIG | Origin | Char | Record Qualifier | Req |
| QEVAL | Evaluator | Char | Record Qualifier | Exp (CT: C78735) |

**[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md; model/06_relationship_datasets.md §6.2]**

### Structure

- **One record per supplemental qualifier per related parent domain record(s)** **[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md §6.2]**
- There is a **one-to-one correspondence** between a domain dataset and its Supplemental Qualifier dataset. The single SUPPQUAL dataset option from SDTMIG v3.1 was **deprecated**. Each domain's supplemental qualifiers are submitted in a separate dataset named `SUPP--` (e.g., `suppae.xpt`, `suppcm.xpt`). **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md §8.4.2]**
- A record in a SUPP-- dataset relates back to its parent record(s) via the key: **STUDYID, RDOMAIN, USUBJID, and IDVAR/IDVARVAL**. An exception is DM records, where both IDVAR and IDVARVAL are null because STUDYID, RDOMAIN, and USUBJID are sufficient to identify the unique parent record. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md §Key Rules]**

---

## When to Use Supplemental Qualifiers

Supplemental qualifiers should be used when:

1. **Sponsor-defined variables need to be captured** that are not part of the standard SDTM domain model. The SDTM does not allow adding new variables to standard domains. **[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md]**

2. **Capturing attributions** — interpretations or subjective classifications of observations by a specific evaluator (e.g., a flag indicating whether an observation was considered clinically significant). **[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md]**

3. **Secondary evaluations** — when observations have primary and secondary evaluations of specific qualifier variables. The primary evaluation goes into the standard domain dataset; the secondary evaluation goes into SUPP--. QNAM is formed by appending "1" to the standard domain variable name (or replacing the last character if the name is already 8 characters). **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.5.4]**

4. **Text strings exceeding 200 characters** — the first 200 characters go in the parent domain variable; each additional 200 characters go in a SUPP-- record. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.5.3.2]**

5. **Multiple values for a non-result qualifier variable** — when a variable can have multiple values (e.g., multiple reasons for a single observation). **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.5.3.2]**

---

## When NOT to Use Supplemental Qualifiers

The following data should **not** be submitted as supplemental qualifiers **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md §8.4.4]**:

- **Subject-level objective data** that fit in Subject Characteristics (SC; e.g., national origin, twin type)
- **Findings interpretations** that should be added as an additional test code and result (e.g., ECG interpretation where EGTESTCD = "INTP")
- **Comments** related to a record or records — these should be captured in the CO special-purpose domain
- **Data not directly related to records in a parent domain** — these should be captured in a separate general observation class domain or special-purpose domain

---

## Key Rules

- **All records must have a value for QVAL** — no records can be in SUPP-- with a null value for QVAL. Transposing source variables with missing/null values may generate SUPP-- records with null QVAL; these must be deleted prior to submission. **[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md — QVAL; chapters/ch08_relationships.md §Key Rules]**
- **QNAM cannot be longer than 8 characters**, cannot start with a number, and cannot contain characters other than letters, numbers, or underscores. **[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md — QNAM]**
- **QLABEL cannot be longer than 40 characters**. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md §8.4.1]**
- **QEVAL** is used only for subjective results (assigned by a person or group). For objective data, QEVAL should be null. **[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md — QEVAL]**
- The combined set of values for **STUDYID, RDOMAIN, USUBJID, IDVAR, IDVARVAL, and QNAM** should be unique for every record. **[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md]**

Based on the retrieved context, the EPOCH variable is used across multiple SDTM domains as a Timing variable. Its purpose is to identify the study epoch (e.g., "SCREENING", "TREATMENT", "FOLLOW-UP") associated with an observation.

## Domains Using EPOCH

The following domains are explicitly documented as using the EPOCH variable:

| Domain | Source |

| **SR** (Skin Response) | [Source: domains/SR/spec.md] |
| **CP** (Cell Phenotype Findings) | [Source: domains/CP/spec.md] |

| **PC** (Pharmacokinetics Concentrations) | [Source: domains/PC/spec.md] |
| **EC** (Exposure as Collected) | [Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md — EC] |
| **EX** (Exposure) | [Source: domains/TA/assumptions.md] |
| **DS** (Disposition) | [Source: domains/TA/assumptions.md] |

## EPOCH Variable Specification

- **Label:** Epoch
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Timing
- **Core:** Perm (Permissible)
- **Controlled Terms:** C99079
- **CDISC Notes:** Epoch associated with the date/time of the observation. Examples: "SCREENING", "TREATMENT", "FOLLOW-UP". [Source: domains/SR/spec.md, domains/FA/spec.md]

## Purpose and Usage Rules

1. **Basis for assignment:**
   - For **Findings class domains**, EPOCH should be based on the `--DTC` variable (date/time of the test or specimen collection). [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.3.1]
   - For **Interventions or Events class domains**, EPOCH should be based on the `--STDTC` variable (start of the intervention or event). [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.3.1]

2. **No imputation:** Sponsors should not impute EPOCH values. Assignment should be based on CRF instructions and structure where possible. If epoch cannot be determined, EPOCH should be null. [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.3.1]

3. **Pre-study observations:** EPOCH is not applicable to interventions, events, or findings that occurred before the subject's participation in a study (including screening, which occurs before RFSTDTC). For such records, EPOCH should be null. [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.3.1]

4. **Distinct values:** In crossover trials with multiple treatment epochs, each must be given a distinct name (e.g., not all called "TREATMENT"). [Source: domains/TA/assumptions.md]

5. **Applicability to general observation classes:** As a Timing variable, EPOCH is permissible for use in any dataset based on a general observation class (Interventions, Events, Findings). [Source: model/02_observation_classes.md]

6. **Not applicable to:** Timing variables cannot be added to SUPPQUAL datasets or RELREC. [Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.3]

Based on the retrieved context, **USUBJID** serves as a linking key across SDTM domains primarily as an **Identifier** variable that uniquely identifies a subject across all studies and applications. Here is how it functions across different domain types:

## Definition and Core Role

USUBJID is defined as:

- **Label:** Unique Subject Identifier
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Identifier
- **Core:** Req (Required) in most domains; Exp (Expected) in RELSUB
- **Controlled Terms:** None

**[Source: domains/DM/spec.md; domains/AE/spec.md; domains/PP/spec.md; domains/CO/spec.md; domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md; domains/RELSPEC/spec.md; domains/RELSUB/spec.md]**

**CDISC Notes:** "Identifier used to uniquely identify a subject across all studies for all applications or submissions involving the product." In DM, it is further specified that "This must be a unique value, and could be a compound identifier formed by concatenating STUDYID-SITEID-SUBJID." **[Source: domains/DM/spec.md]**

## How USUBJID Links Across Domains

### 1. As a Primary Key Component in Special-Purpose Domains

USUBJID is part of the natural key structure for special-purpose domains:

| Domain | Key Structure |
|--------|--------------|
| DM | STUDYID, USUBJID |
| SE | STUDYID, USUBJID, ETCD, SESTDTC |
| SM | STUDYID, USUBJID, MIDS |
| SV | STUDYID, USUBJID, SVTERM |
| CO | STUDYID, USUBJID, IDVAR, COREF, COOTC |

**[Source: chapters/ch03_submitting_data.md]**

### 2. As a Key in General Observation Class Domains

USUBJID is a required identifier in all general observation class datasets (Interventions, Events, Findings), enabling record-level linkage across domains for the same subject. For example:

- **AE (Adverse Events):** STUDYID, USUBJID, AESEQ
- **CM (Concomitant Medications):** STUDYID, USUBJID, CMTRT, CMSTDTC
- **AG (Procedure Agents):** STUDYID, USUBJID, AGTRT, AGSTDTC

**[Source: chapters/ch03_submitting_data.md]**

### 3. In Relationship Datasets

- **RELREC:** USUBJID and IDVARVAL are **null** for dataset-to-dataset relationships (e.g., TU to TR), because RELREC links datasets, not individual subject records. However, within-subject relationships use USUBJID as part of the key. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md]**
- **RELSPEC:** USUBJID is a required Identifier (Core: Req). **[Source: domains/RELSPEC/spec.md]**
- **RELSUB:** USUBJID is Expected (Core: Exp), with the note "Either USUBJID or POOLID must be populated." **[Source: domains/RELSUB/spec.md]**

### 4. In Supplemental Qualifiers (SUPP--)

USUBJID is used to identify the parent record(s) to which supplemental qualifier values belong. The SUPPQUAL spec notes: "This is the value of USUBJID in the parent record(s)." **[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md]**

### 5. In Associated Persons (AP) Domains

For associated persons data, **APID** is used instead of USUBJID. The linking variable **RSUBJID** may be populated with the USUBJID of the related subject to establish the relationship between an associated person and a study subject. **[Source: model/04_associated_persons.md]**

## Summary

USUBJID serves as the **universal subject identifier** that:
1. Uniquely identifies a subject across all studies and submissions
2. Forms part of the natural key in every subject-level domain
3. Enables cross-domain record linkage (e.g., linking AE records to CM records for the same subject)
4. Is referenced in relationship datasets (RELSPEC, RELSUB) and supplemental qualifiers (SUPP--)
5. Is replaced by APID in associated persons domains, with RSUBJID optionally carrying the USUBJID value for linkage

results.answer:
Based on the retrieved context, adverse events (AE) are linked to concomitant medications (CM) using the **RELREC** (Related Records) special-purpose dataset. This is done by creating records in RELREC that share a common **RELID** value for the related AE and CM records within the same **USUBJID**.

Here is the detailed mechanism:

1.  **When to use RELREC:** The AE domain assumption states that if a non-study treatment (concomitant medication) is given because of an adverse event, the treatment information is represented in the CM domain and "linked to the AE record with RELREC" **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md -- item_6]**. This is an example of an "explicit relationship" as described in the RELREC assumptions **[Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md -- overview]**.

2.  **How the link is established:** A relationship is defined by adding a record to RELREC for each record to be related (one for the AE, one for the CM) and assigning a unique character identifier value for the relationship, stored in the **RELID** variable. The value of RELID must be identical for all related records within a USUBJID **[Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md -- overview]**.

3.  **Key variables in RELREC:**
    - **STUDYID, USUBJID:** Identify the study and subject.
    - **RDOMAIN:** The domain code of the record in the relationship (e.g., "AE" or "CM") **[Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md -- overview]**.
    - **IDVAR:** The variable used to identify the specific record within the domain (e.g., "AESEQ" for the AE record's sequence number, or "CMSEQ" for the CM record's sequence number) **[Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md -- overview]**.
    - **IDVARVAL:** The value of the variable described in IDVAR (e.g., the specific sequence number like "5" for the AE or "11" for the CM) **[Source: domains/RELREC/assumptions.md -- overview]**.
    - **RELID:** The relationship identifier that groups the related records together.

4.  **Example from the context:**
    The following example from the RELREC examples shows an AE record (AESEQ=5) related to two CM records (CMSEQ=11 and CMSEQ=12) using RELID="1" **[Source: domains/RELREC/examples.md -- Peer Record Examples]**.

    | Row | STUDYID | RDOMAIN | USUBJID | IDVAR | IDVARVAL | RELTYPE | RELID |
    |-----|---------|---------|---------|-------|----------|---------|-------|
    | 1 | EFC1234 | AE | 123456 | AESEQ | 5 | | 1 |
    | 2 | EFC1234 | CM | 123456 | CMSEQ | 11 | | 1 |
    | 3 | EFC1234 | CM | 123456 | CMSEQ | 12 | | 1 |

5.  **Alternative using --GRPID:** If the concomitant medications are already grouped within the CM domain using a variable like **CMGRPID**, the relationship can be represented more efficiently. Instead of listing each CM record individually, the RELREC record can use `IDVAR="CMGRPID"` and `IDVARVAL="COMBO1"` to relate the AE to the entire group of medications **[Source: domains/RELREC/examples.md -- Peer Record Examples]**.

    | Row | STUDYID | RDOMAIN | USUBJID | IDVAR | IDVARVAL | RELTYPE | RELID |
    |-----|---------|---------|---------|-------|----------|---------|-------|
    | 1 | EFC1234 | AE | 123456 | AESEQ | 5 | | 1 |
    | 2 | EFC1234 | CM | 123456 | CMGRPID | COMBO1 | | 1 |

In summary, the link is made by creating a set of records in the RELREC dataset that share a common RELID, with each record pointing to a specific record in either the AE or CM domain using the RDOMAIN, IDVAR, and IDVARVAL variables.

## TR–RS Linkage in Oncology Studies

The TR (Tumor/Lesion Results) and RS (Disease Response) domains are linked through a **RELREC dataset-to-dataset relationship** using the `--LNKGRP` variable in both domains. This is a **bidirectional linkage** that connects individual tumor/lesion measurements/assessments in TR to the response evaluation records in RS.

---

### Linkage Mechanism

**Variable used:** `RSLNKGRP` (in RS) and `TRLNKGRP` (in TR)

Both variables serve as the grouping identifier that supports a RELREC relationship. The values in `RSLNKGRP` and `TRLNKGRP` must match to establish the link.

**Source:** [domains/RS/assumptions.md — item_4]  
**Source:** [domains/TR/assumptions.md — item_2]

---

### Direction 1: TR → RS (Tumor Results to Response Assessment)

| Domain | Variable | Role | Description |
|--------|----------|------|-------------|
| TR | `TRLNKGRP` | Record Qualifier | Provides a unique code for each response and associated tumor/lesion measurements/assessments. Used to relate TR records to a response assessment record in RS. |

**Rule:** A RELREC relationship must exist to link the related data rows. A dataset-to-dataset link is the most appropriate mechanism. The `--LNKGRP` variable is used because `--GRPID`, `--REFID`, and `--SPID` may be used for other purposes per SDTM.

**Source:** [domains/TR/assumptions.md — item_2]

---

### Direction 2: RS → TR (Response Assessment to Source Tumor Results)

| Domain | Variable | Role | Description |
|--------|----------|------|-------------|
| RS | `RSLNKGRP` | Record Qualifier | Provides a link between the records in a findings domain (e.g., TR, LB) that contribute to a record in the RS domain. |

**Rule:** Records should exist in the RELREC dataset to support this relationship. A RELREC relationship could also be defined using `RSLNKID` when a response evaluation or clinical classification measure relates back to another source dataset (e.g., tumor assessment in TR).

**Source:** [domains/RS/assumptions.md — item_4]

---

### Example of the Linkage

From the RS examples, the linkage is demonstrated:

| Row | RSLNKGRP | RSTESTCD | RSTEST | RSSTRESC |
|-----|----------|----------|--------|----------|
| 3 | A2 | OVRLRESP | Overall Response | PR |
| 7 | A3 | OVRLRESP | Overall Response | PD |

The `RSLNKGRP` value (e.g., "A2", "A3") would match corresponding `TRLNKGRP` values in the TR domain to link the overall response assessment to the underlying tumor measurements that contributed to that assessment.

**Source:** [domains/RS/examples.md — Example 1]

---

### Additional Linkage: TU → TR (Tumor Identification to Tumor Results)

While not directly TR→RS, the **TU (Tumor/Lesion Identification) domain** links to TR via `TULNKID` / `TRLNKID`, and this chain ultimately supports the RS linkage:

| Domain Pair | Variable Pair | Mechanism |
|-------------|---------------|-----------|
| TU → TR | `TULNKID` ↔ `TRLNKID` | RELREC dataset-to-dataset link |
| TR → RS | `TRLNKGRP` ↔ `RSLNKGRP` | RELREC dataset-to-dataset link |

**Source:** [domains/TU/assumptions.md — item_2]  
**Source:** [domains/TR/assumptions.md — item_1]

---

### Summary Table

| Linkage Direction | Source Variable | Target Variable | Mechanism |
|-------------------|----------------|-----------------|-----------|
| TR → RS | `TRLNKGRP` | `RSLNKGRP` | RELREC dataset-to-dataset |
| RS → TR | `RSLNKGRP` | `TRLNKGRP` | RELREC dataset-to-dataset |
| TU → TR | `TULNKID` | `TRLNKID` | RELREC dataset-to-dataset |

**Key point:** The `--LNKGRP` variables (not `--LNKID`) are the specific identifiers used for the TR–RS linkage. The `--LNKID` variables are used for the TU–TR linkage. Both require corresponding records in the RELREC domain.

## FA (Findings About Events or Interventions) Domain

### Overview

The FA domain is a **Findings About** subtype of the Findings observation class, used to record findings about observations in the Interventions or Events classes. **[Source: model/02_observation_classes.md]**

### Variable Specification (Key Variables)

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core | Controlled Terms |
|----------|-------|------|------|------|-----------------|
| FATESTCD | Findings About Test Short Name | Char | Topic | Req | C101832 |
| FATEST | Findings About Test Name | Char | Synonym Qualifier | Req | C101833 |
| FAOBJ | Object of the Observation | Char | Record Qualifier | Req | — |
| FASEQ | Sequence Number | Num | Identifier | Req | — |
| FAORRES | Result or Finding in Original Units | Char | Result Qualifier | Exp | — |
| FASTRESC | Character Result/Finding in Std Format | Char | Result Qualifier | Exp | — |
| FASTRESN | Numeric Result/Finding in Standard Units | Num | Result Qualifier | Perm | — |
| FASTAT | Completion Status | Char | Record Qualifier | Perm | C66789 |
| FADTC | Date/Time of Collection | Char | Timing | Exp | ISO 8601 |

**[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md — FA section]**

### Class Designation

FA is classified as **Findings About**, a subtype of the Findings observation class. The SR (Skin Response) domain shares this same class designation. **[Source: domains/FA/spec.md — Related Domains]**

---

## How FAOBJ Links to Parent Domains

### Mechanism

**FAOBJ** (Object of the Observation) is the variable unique to the Findings About structure. It describes the event or intervention whose property is being measured in FATESTCD/FATEST. **[Source: model/02_observation_classes.md]**

In conjunction with FATESTCD, FAOBJ describes what the topic of the observation is; therefore, **both are required to be populated for every record**. FATESTCD describes the measurement/evaluation and FAOBJ describes the event or intervention that the measurement/evaluation is about. **[Source: model/02_observation_classes.md]**

### How FAOBJ Values Are Derived

The values in FAOBJ are typically the **coded terms** (--DECOD values) from the parent domain record:

- **For AE parent records**: FAOBJ contains the value from **AEDECOD** (e.g., "NAUSEA", "DIARRHEA", "HEADACHE") **[Source: domains/FA/examples.md — Example 6]**
- **For CM parent records**: FAOBJ would contain the value from **CMDECOD** (the coded medication name)
- **For PR parent records**: FAOBJ would contain the value from **PRTRT** or the coded procedure term

### Example: FAOBJ Linking to AE

In Example 6 (severity assessments over time):

| FATESTCD | FATEST | FAOBJ | FAORRES | FASPID |
|----------|--------|-------|---------|--------|
| SEV | Severity/Intensity | Nausea | MILD | 1 |
| SEV | Severity/Intensity | Nausea | MODERATE | 1 |
| SEV | Severity/Intensity | Diarrhea | MILD | 2 |

Here, FAOBJ="NAUSEA" matches AEDECOD in the AE domain, and FASPID matches AESPID to link the FA records to specific AE records. **[Source: domains/FA/examples.md — Example 6]**

### Example: FAOBJ for Prespecified AEs

In Example 4 (occurrence of prespecified AEs):

| FATESTCD | FATEST | FAOBJ | FAORRES |
|----------|--------|-------|---------|
| OCCUR | Occurrence Indicator | Headache | Y |
| OCCUR | Occurrence Indicator | Respiratory Infection | N |
| OCCUR | Occurrence Indicator | Nausea | NOT DONE |

FAOBJ contains the prespecified AE term name. When FAORRES="Y", a corresponding AE record exists with AEPRESP="Y". **[Source: domains/FA/examples.md — Example 4]**

---

## When to Use FA (Three Criteria)

Per Section 6.4.1, FA should be used when:

1. **Criterion 1**: Data or observations that have **different timing from an associated event or intervention as a whole** (e.g., severity assessed at each visit for an ongoing AE)
2. **Criterion 2**: An observation about an event or intervention which requires **more than 1 variable** for its representation (e.g., rash diameter + unit + lesion counts)
3. **Criterion 3**: Data that indicate the **occurrence of prespecified AEs** (solicited at each visit)

**[Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md — item_6]**

---

## Related Domains

FA can link to the following parent domains:

| Parent Domain | Relationship |
|---------------|--------------|
| AE | Findings about adverse events |
| CM | Findings about concomitant medications |
| PR | Findings about procedures |
| EX | Findings about exposure |
| EC | Findings about exposure as collected |
| ML | Findings about meals |
| SU | Findings about substance use |

**[Source: domains/FA/spec.md — Related Domains]**

---

## Key Restrictions

- The following qualifiers should **generally not be used** in FA: --BODSYS, --MODIFY, --SEV, --TOXGR **[Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md — item_6]**
- When FATESTCD values match variable names from parent domains (e.g., SEV, OCCUR, TOXGR), the FATEST should use the corresponding variable label **[Source: model/02_observation_classes.md]**
- FAOBJ is **Required** (Core: Req) — every FA record must specify what event or intervention it is about **[Source: domains/FA/spec.md — FAOBJ]**

results.answer:
# How TA, TE, TV, and TI Work Together to Define a Study Design

The four Trial Design domains form a hierarchical, interconnected model that describes a clinical trial's planned conduct. Here is how they relate:

## 1. TE (Trial Elements) — The Building Blocks

TE defines the **atomic time periods** (elements) that serve a purpose in the trial. Each element appears once in TE, regardless of how many times it is reused across arms.

**Key variables:** ETCD (Element Code), ELEMENT (Description), TESTRL (Start Rule), TEENRL (End Rule), TEDUR (Planned Duration)

> *"An element is a building block for creating study cells, and an arm is composed of study cells."* **[Source: domains/TE/assumptions.md]**

**Example elements:** Screen, Run-In, Placebo, Drug A, Drug B

## 2. TA (Trial Arms) — The Ordered Sequence

TA defines **each planned arm** as an ordered sequence of elements. It connects elements into complete subject paths through the trial.

**Key variables:** ARMCD/ARM (Arm), TAETORD (Order within Arm), ETCD/ELEMENT (referencing TE), TABRANCH (Branch rules), TATRANS (Transition rules), EPOCH

> *"An arm is a planned path through the trial. This path covers the entire time of the trial."* **[Source: domains/TA/assumptions.md]**

**How TA references TE:** TA uses `ETCD` to reference elements defined in TE. The same element (e.g., "Screen") can appear in multiple arms and multiple positions within an arm. **[Source: model/05_study_level_data.md]**

**Example:** In a 3-arm parallel trial, TA contains 3 arms × 3 elements = 9 records, while TE contains only 5 unique elements. **[Source: domains/TE/assumptions.md]**

## 3. TV (Trial Visits) — The Data Collection Schedule

TV defines **planned visits** where data collection occurs, referencing the epochs (and sometimes elements) defined in TA.

**Key variables:** VISITNUM, VISIT, TVSTRL (Start Rule), TVENRL (End Rule)

> *"Visits can span epoch transitions... the transition event that marks the beginning of the run-in epoch occurs during visit 2."* **[Source: domains/TV/examples.md]**

**How TV references TA:** TV start/end rules reference epochs (e.g., "Start of Screen Epoch", "30 minutes after start of Treatment Epoch"). When epochs span multiple elements, TV rules may need to reference elements and TAETORD. **[Source: domains/TV/examples.md]**

## 4. TI (Trial Inclusion/Exclusion) — Subject Eligibility

TI defines **all inclusion and exclusion criteria** for the trial, which determine which subjects can enter the trial design defined by TA/TE/TV.

**Key variables:** IETESTCD, IETEST, IECAT, TIRL

> *"TI contains all the inclusion and exclusion criteria for the trial, and thus provides information that may not be present in the subject-level data."* **[Source: domains/TI/assumptions.md]**

## How They Interconnect

```
TE (Elements) ──referenced by──→ TA (Arms) ──defines epochs──→ TV (Visits)
                                    │
                                    └── subjects must satisfy ──→ TI (Eligibility)
```

1. **TE → TA:** TE defines reusable elements; TA assembles them into ordered arm sequences using `ETCD` as the foreign key. **[Source: model/05_study_level_data.md]**

2. **TA → TV:** TA defines epochs (e.g., Screening, Run-In, Treatment); TV visits are scheduled relative to epoch boundaries. **[Source: domains/TV/examples.md]**

3. **TI → All:** TI defines who can enter the trial; the IE domain (subject-level) records which criteria were not met. **[Source: domains/TI/assumptions.md]**

4. **All are Trial Design domains:** TA, TD, TE, TI, TM, TS, and TV share the same class (Trial Design). **[Source: domains/TA/spec.md, domains/TE/spec.md, domains/TV/spec.md, domains/TI/spec.md]**

## Practical Example (from TA Example 1)

For a 3-arm parallel trial:

- **TE** defines 5 unique elements: Screen, Run-In, Placebo, Drug A, Drug B
- **TA** defines 3 arms, each with 3 elements in order: Screen → Run-In → (Placebo | Drug A | Drug B)
- **TV** defines 5 visits, with Visit 2 spanning Screen→Run-In transition and Visit 3 spanning Run-In→Treatment transition
- **TI** defines the inclusion/exclusion criteria that subjects must meet before entering the Screen element

**[Source: domains/TA/examples.md, domains/TV/examples.md]**

## CO (Comments) Domain Overview

The **Comments (CO)** domain is a **Special-Purpose** domain used to capture unstructured free-text comments that are not part of normal domain data. Comments are normally supplied by a principal investigator but may also be collected from other sources such as central reviewers. **[Source: model/03_special_purpose_domains.md]**

### Structure
- **One record per comment per subject** (or per study)
- Contains **15 variables** in the SDTM v2.0 model
- Key variables include: STUDYID, DOMAIN, RDOMAIN, USUBJID, COSEQ, IDVAR, IDVARVAL, COREF, COVAL, COEVAL, COEVALID, CODTC, CODY **[Source: model/03_special_purpose_domains.md]**

### Variable Definitions (Selected)

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core | Controlled Terms |
|----------|-------|------|------|------|-----------------|
| COSEQ | Sequence Number | Num | Identifier | Req | — |
| COREF | Comment Reference | Char | Record Qualifier | Perm | — |
| COVAL | Comment | Char | Topic | Req | — |
| COEVAL | Evaluator | Char | Record Qualifier | Perm | C78735 |
| COEVALID | Evaluator Identifier | Char | Record Qualifier | Perm | C96777 |
| CODTC | Date/Time of Comment | Char | Timing | Perm | ISO 8601 datetime or interval |
| CODY | Study Day of Comment | Num | Timing | Perm | — |

**[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md — CO]**

---

## RDOMAIN and IDVAR Mechanism

The CO domain uses the **same key structure** as Supplemental Qualifiers (SUPP--) to identify related parent records. The key variables are: **STUDYID, RDOMAIN, USUBJID, IDVAR, and IDVARVAL**. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md §8.5]**

### Three Levels of Relationship

The CO dataset accommodates **3 sources of comments**, determined by how RDOMAIN, IDVAR, and IDVARVAL are populated: **[Source: domains/CO/assumptions.md — item_3]**

#### 1. Comments unrelated to any specific domain or parent record
- **RDOMAIN** = null
- **IDVAR** = null
- **IDVARVAL** = null
- **CODTC** should be populated if captured
- *Example:* A comment collected on a separate comments page

#### 2. Comments related to a domain but not to specific parent record(s)
- **RDOMAIN** = DOMAIN code of the parent domain (e.g., "PE", "AE")
- **IDVAR** = null
- **IDVARVAL** = null
- **CODTC** should be populated if captured
- *Example:* A comment collected at the bottom of the PE page for Visit 7, without indication of specific records

#### 3. Comments related to a specific parent record or group of parent records
- **RDOMAIN** = DOMAIN code of the parent record(s)
- **IDVAR** = key variable name of the parent record (e.g., "AESEQ", "EXGRPID", "VSGRPID")
- **IDVARVAL** = value of the variable described in IDVAR (e.g., "7", "COMBO1", "VS2")
- **CODTC** should be **null** because the timing of the parent record(s) is inherited by the comment record

### IDVAR Usage Examples

| IDVAR Value | IDVARVAL Example | Meaning |
|-------------|------------------|---------|
| AESEQ | 7 | Comment relates to a single AE record with AESEQ=7 |
| EXGRPID | COMBO1 | Comment relates to multiple EX records grouped by EXGRPID="COMBO1" |
| VSGRPID | VS2 | Comment relates to multiple VS records grouped by VSGRPID="VS2" |
| VISITNUM | 4 | Comment relates to a specific visit (when RDOMAIN="SV") |

**[Source: domains/CO/examples.md — Example 1]**

### Additional Notes

- **COREF** can be used to capture additional information about the comment relationship (e.g., CRF page number or name) that cannot be represented using RDOMAIN, IDVAR, and IDVARVAL alone. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md §8.5]**
- **Timing variables** (e.g., VISITNUM, VISIT) may be added to the CO domain. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md §8.5]**
- A single comment may only be related to a group of records in **1 domain** (RDOMAIN can have only 1 value). If a single comment relates to records in multiple domains, the comment may need to be repeated in CO. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md §8.5]**
- When comment text exceeds **200 characters**, the first 200 characters go in COVAL, the next 200 in COVAL1, and so on (COVALn). **[Source: domains/CO/assumptions.md — item_4]**
- Comments should **not** be submitted as supplemental qualifiers; they belong in the CO domain. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md §8.4.4]**

results.answer:
## EC vs EX: Purpose and Usage

### Core Distinction

**EC (Exposure as Collected)** represents protocol-specified study treatment administrations **as they are actually collected** from the source (e.g., CRF, dispensing log). The unit of measurement is the collected unit (e.g., tablets, mL), which may differ from the protocol-specified unit.

**EX (Exposure)** represents study treatment administrations **in the protocol-specified unit** (e.g., mg, mg/kg). EX is recognized in most cases as a **derived dataset**, where EXDOSU reflects the protocol-specified unit per study treatment. **[Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_1b]**

---

### When to Use EC

EC **should** be used when collected exposure information cannot or should not be directly represented in EX. Specific examples include:

- Administrations collected in **tablets** when the protocol-specified unit is **mg**
- Administrations collected in **mL** when the protocol-specified unit is **mg/kg**
- Any case where the collected unit differs from the analysis unit

**[Source: domains/EC/assumptions.md -- item_1a]**

EC is **optional** (at sponsor's discretion) only if the entire EC dataset is an exact duplicate of the entire EX dataset. **[Source: domains/EC/assumptions.md -- item_1b]**

Collected exposure log data points descriptive of administrations typically reflect amounts at the **product-level** (e.g., number of tablets, number of mL). **[Source: domains/EC/assumptions.md -- item_1c]**

Product accountability details (e.g., amount dispensed, amount returned) are represented in the **DA** domain, **not** in EC. **[Source: domains/EC/assumptions.md -- item_1a]**

---

### When to Use EX

EX is **required** for all studies that include protocol-specified study treatment. **[Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_1c]**

EX should contain **1 record per constant-dosing interval per subject**. The constant-dosing interval is sponsor-defined and may include any period of time described in terms of a known treatment given at a consistent dose, frequency, infusion rate, etc. **[Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_1d]**

Common methods for determining exposure (from most direct to least direct):
1. Derived from actual observation of administration by the investigator
2. Derived from automated dispensing device that records administrations
3. Derived from subject recall
4. Derived from product accountability data
5. Derived from the protocol

**[Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_1c]**

Treatments that are **not protocol-specified** should be represented in **CM** (Concomitant/Prior Medications) or another Interventions domain, **not** in EX. **[Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_1a]**

---

### Relationship Between EC and EX

When both EC and EX are implemented, the relationship between them can be described in **RELREC** when it should be defined. EX derivations must be described in the **Define-XML** document. **[Source: domains/EC/assumptions.md -- item_6; domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_5]**

When EC is implemented with EX:
- **EXVAMT and EXVAMTU** would **not** be used in EX; collected values instead are represented in **ECDOSE and ECDOSU** (and ECVAMT and ECVAMTU as needed). **[Source: domains/EX/assumptions.md -- item_6c]**

---

### Practical Example

From the examples, a study with weekly infusions of Drug Z 10 mg/kg:

- **EC** records show both **intended doses** (in mg/kg, with ECMOOD = "SCHEDULED") and **actual administered amounts** (in mL, with ECMOOD = "PERFORMED"), plus concentration in mg/mL
- **EX** records show only the **actual doses administered** in the protocol-specified unit (mg/kg), with no record for doses that were not given

**[Source: domains/EX/examples.md -- Example 7]**

---

### Summary Table

| Aspect | EC | EX |
|--------|----|----|
| **Purpose** | Collected data as-is | Derived data in protocol-specified unit |
| **Unit** | Collected unit (tablets, mL) | Protocol-specified unit (mg, mg/kg) |
| **Nature** | Source data | Derived dataset |
| **Required?** | Optional if identical to EX | Required for protocol-specified treatment |
| **Records** | Per collected administration | Per constant-dosing interval |
| **Missed doses** | Can include (ECOCCUR = "N") | Generally not included |
| **Class** | Interventions | Interventions |

## VISIT and VISITNUM Usage Across Observation-Class Domains

### VISITNUM — Consistent Definition and Role

VISITNUM is defined consistently across all observation-class domains (Interventions, Events, and Findings) with the same Label, Type, Role, and Core:

- **Label:** Visit Number
- **Type:** Num
- **Role:** Timing
- **Core:** Exp (Expected)
- **Controlled Terms:** None (free numeric)
- **CDISC Notes:** "Clinical encounter number. Numeric version of VISIT, used for sorting."

This definition appears identically in domains such as:
- **FA** (Findings About) — Order 24, Role Timing, Core Exp **[Source: domains/FA/spec.md]**
- **AG** (Procedure Agents, Interventions) — Order 26, Role Timing, Core Exp **[Source: domains/AG/spec.md]**
- **PE** (Physical Examination, Findings) — Order 24, Role Timing, Core Exp **[Source: domains/PE/spec.md]**

### VISIT — Consistent Definition

VISIT is also consistent across domains:

- **Label:** Visit Name
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Timing
- **Core:** Perm (Permissible)
- **CDISC Notes:** "1. Protocol-defined description of clinical encounter. 2. May be used in addition to VISITNUM and/or VISITDY."

**[Source: domains/AG/spec.md]**

### Key Usage Rules

1. **One-to-one relationship between VISIT and VISITNUM** — There must be a one-to-one relationship between VISIT and VISITNUM for planned visits. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.4.5]**

2. **Planned visits must use TV values** — For planned visits, values of VISIT, VISITNUM, and VISITDY must be those defined in the Trial Visits (TV) dataset. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.4.5]**

3. **Unplanned visits** — Any values of VISITNUM that appear in subject-level datasets that are not in the TV dataset are assumed to correspond to unplanned visits. **[Source: domains/TV/assumptions.md item_6]**

4. **VISITDY restriction** — VISITDY must **not** be populated for unplanned visits; the actual study day of an unplanned visit belongs in a `--DY` variable. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.4.5]**

5. **Unplanned visit VISITNUM assignment** — The easiest method is to assign the same value (e.g., 99) to all unplanned visits, though this provides no chronological sorting. More sophisticated methods require knowing all unplanned visits for a subject. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.4.5]**

---

## Role of the SV (Subject Visits) Domain

### Structure and Purpose

- **Class:** Special Purpose
- **Structure:** One record per actual or planned visit per subject
- **Primary Keys:** STUDYID, USUBJID, SVTERM **[Source: chapters/ch03_submitting_data.md §3.2.1]**

The SV dataset provides a summary of a subject's visits over the course of their participation in a study. Comparison of an individual subject's SV dataset with the TV dataset (planned visits) supports the identification of planned but not completed visits. **[Source: domains/SV/assumptions.md]**

### Actual Visit Date Tracking

SV captures **actual** visit dates through two timing variables:

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core |
|----------|-------|------|------|------|
| **SVSTDTC** | Start Date/Time of Observation | Char | Timing | Exp |
| **SVENDTC** | End Date/Time of Observation | Char | Timing | Exp |
| **SVSTDY** | Study Day of Start of Observation | Num | Timing | Perm |
| **SVENDY** | Study Day of End of Observation | Num | Timing | Perm |

**[Source: model/03_special_purpose_domains.md; domains/SV/spec.md]**

### Key SV-Specific Variables

| Variable | Label | Role | Core | Notes |
|----------|-------|------|------|-------|
| **SVPRESP** | Pre-specified | Variable Qualifier | Exp | Controlled by C66742 (NY) |
| **SVOCCUR** | Occurrence | Record Qualifier | Exp | Controlled by C66742 (NY) |
| **SVREASOC** | Reason for Occur Value | Record Qualifier | Perm | Free text |
| **SVCNTMOD** | Contact Mode | Record Qualifier | Perm | Controlled by C171445 |
| **SVEPCHGI** | Epi/Pandemic Related Change Indicator | Record Qualifier | Perm | Controlled by C66742 (NY) |
| **SVUPDES** | Description of Unplanned Visit | Record Qualifier | Perm | Free text |

**[Source: domains/SV/spec.md]**

### How SV Relates to Observation-Class Domains

1. **Planned vs. Actual Comparison** — Comparison of SVSTDY and SVENDY to VISIT and/or VISITDY can highlight departures from the planned timing of visits. **[Source: domains/SV/assumptions.md]**

2. **Unplanned Visit Handling** — Records for unplanned visits should be included in the SV dataset. SVUPDES can be populated with a description of the reason for the unplanned visit. If data from an encounter are included in any domain for which VISITNUM is included, the encounter should generally be treated as a visit and included in SV. **[Source: domains/SV/assumptions.md item_6]**

3. **Consistency with TV** — The method for deriving SV values should be consistent with the visit definitions in the TV dataset. **[Source: domains/SV/assumptions.md]**

4. **VISITNUM as the Link** — VISITNUM serves as the common key linking SV (actual visit dates) to observation-class domains (data collected at those visits). For planned visits, VISITNUM values in SV must match those in TV; for unplanned visits, VISITNUM values are assigned per sponsor practice and must be consistent across all domains. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.4.5]**

---

## Summary

VISITNUM and VISIT are **Timing role** variables used consistently across all Interventions, Events, and Findings domains with identical definitions (Label, Type, Role, Core). The SV domain plays a complementary role by tracking **actual** visit start/end dates (SVSTDTC, SVENDTC) and study days (SVSTDY, SVENDY) for each subject, enabling comparison against the planned schedule in TV. VISITNUM serves as the common identifier linking SV records to observation-class domain records, with unplanned visits requiring special handling for VISITNUM assignment and VISITDY exclusion.

# RELSPEC Domain Overview

## What is RELSPEC?

**RELSPEC** (Related Specimens) is a **Relationship** class dataset used to describe relationships between **specimens**, enabling representation of specimen lineage (e.g., parent specimen to derived aliquots or processed specimens). **[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md]**

### Variable Specification

| # | Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core | Notes |
|---|----------|-------|------|------|------|-------|
| 1 | STUDYID | Study Identifier | Char | Identifier | Req | |
| 2 | USUBJID | Unique Subject Identifier | Char | Identifier | Req | |
| 3 | REFID | Reference ID | Char | Identifier | Req | C82531 |
| 4 | SPEC | Specimen Type | Char | Variable Qualifier (REFID) | Exp | C70713 |
| 5 | PARENT | Specimen Parent | Char | Identifier | Exp | Identifies the REFID of the parent of a specimen to support tracking its genealogy |
| 6 | LEVEL | Specimen Level | Num | Variable Qualifier (REFID) | Exp | Identifies the generation number of the sample where the collected sample is considered the first generation |

**[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md]**

---

## Key Distinction: RELSPEC vs. RELREC

### RELSPEC — Specimen Lineage Only

- **Purpose:** Maintains relationships **between specimens** (parent-child lineage, e.g., whole blood → plasma aliquot)
- **Scope:** Does **not** manage relationships between any other datasets or domains **[Source: domains/RELSPEC/assumptions.md, item 1]**
- **Structure:** One record per specimen identifier per subject **[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md]**
- **Variables:** Does **not** require additional variables such as those used in RELREC (e.g., no RDOMAIN, IDVAR, IDVARVAL, RELID, RELTYPE) **[Source: domains/RELSPEC/assumptions.md, item 2]**
- **Subject-level:** Yes (subject-level data) **[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md]**

### RELREC — Record/Dataset Relationships

- **Purpose:** Links records within a domain, across domains, or between entire datasets **[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md]**
- **Scope:** Can relate peer records (subject-level) **or** entire datasets (study-level, with USUBJID null) **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md]**
- **Structure:** One record per related record, group of records, or dataset **[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md]**
- **Variables:** Uses RDOMAIN, IDVAR, IDVARVAL, RELID, RELTYPE to define relationships **[Source: domains/RELREC/spec.md]**
- **Subject-level:** Both subject-level and dataset-level **[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md]**

---

## Critical Correction to the Question

**RELSPEC does NOT define relationships between datasets at the study level.** It is exclusively for specimen lineage tracking. The dataset that defines relationships between datasets at the study level is **RELREC** (when USUBJID is null and RELTYPE is populated with ONE/MANY). **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md, Section 8.3]**

### How RELREC Defines Dataset-Level Relationships

When RELREC is used for dataset-to-dataset relationships:

- **USUBJID** is null
- **IDVAR** contains the merge key variable name (e.g., TULNKID, TRLNKID)
- **IDVARVAL** is null
- **RELTYPE** identifies the hierarchical level (ONE or MANY)

**Example** (from chapters/ch08_relationships.md):

| STUDYID | RDOMAIN | USUBJID | IDVAR | IDVARVAL | RELTYPE | RELID |
|---------|---------|---------|-------|----------|---------|-------|
| EFC1234 | TU | | TULNKID | | ONE | 1 |
| EFC1234 | TR | | TRLNKID | | MANY | 1 |

This represents a one-to-many relationship between the TU and TR datasets, where TULNKID and TRLNKID are the merge keys.

---

## Summary Table

| Aspect | RELSPEC | RELREC |
|--------|---------|--------|
| **Class** | Relationship | Relationship |
| **Purpose** | Specimen lineage | Record/dataset relationships |
| **Subject-level?** | Yes | Both (subject and dataset) |
| **Can relate datasets?** | **No** | **Yes** (with USUBJID null) |
| **Key variables** | REFID, PARENT, LEVEL, SPEC | RDOMAIN, IDVAR, IDVARVAL, RELID, RELTYPE |
| **Controlled terminology** | SPEC (C77529), SPECTYPE (C78734), GENSMP (C111114) | RELTYPE (ONE/MANY) |

**[Sources: model/06_relationship_datasets.md; domains/RELSPEC/assumptions.md; chapters/ch08_relationships.md]**

results.answer:
## SDTM Core Designations

The **Core** column in SDTM domain models specifies three categories that define whether a variable must be included in a dataset and whether it can contain null values:

### Req (Required)
- **Meaning**: A Required variable is basic to the identification of a data record (i.e., essential key variables and a topic variable) or is necessary to make the record meaningful.
- **Rule**: Must always be included in the dataset and **cannot be null for any record**.
- **Example**: `SRTESTCD` in the SR domain is Req — every record must have a test code. **[Source: domains/SR/spec.md]**

### Exp (Expected)
- **Meaning**: Any variable necessary to make a record useful in the context of a specific domain.
- **Rule**: Must be included in the dataset. Values should be populated when available; null values are allowed when data were not collected or are not applicable. If the study does not include the data item for an expected variable, a null column must still be included in the dataset, and a comment must be included in the Define-XML document stating that the study does not include the data item.
- **Example**: `AEREL` (Causality) in AE is Exp — it must be in the dataset but may be null if causality was not assessed. **[Source: domains/AE/spec.md]**

### Perm (Permissible)
- **Meaning**: May be included in the dataset if the study collected the data.
- **Rule**: 
  - If a study includes a data item that would be represented in a Permissible variable, then that variable **must** be included (even if null) and declared in Define-XML.
  - If a study did **not** collect the data item, the variable should **not** be included in the dataset and should **not** be declared in Define-XML.
- **Example**: `SRGRPID` (Group ID) in SR is Perm — it is included only if the study uses grouping identifiers. **[Source: domains/SR/spec.md]**

### Additional Notes
- All identifier, timing, and general observation class variables listed in the SDTM are permissible unless specifically restricted by the implementation guide or domain assumptions. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.5]**
- Domain assumptions that say a Permissible variable is "generally not used" do **not** prohibit use of the variable. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.5]**
- A null value should not be included in the permissible value set for controlled terminology; null is implied for any list of controlled terms unless the variable is Required. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.3.3]**

## Difference Between Topic, Qualifier, and Identifier Variable Roles

The SDTM defines **5 major variable roles**, of which Identifier, Topic, and Qualifier are three. Each role describes a distinct type of information conveyed by the variable about each observation.

---

### 1. Identifier Variables

**Purpose:** Identify the study, subject, domain, and sequence number of the record.

**Key characteristics:**
- Provide the keys for linking records across datasets
- Typically appear first in the variable ordering for all observation classes
- Examples: `STUDYID`, `DOMAIN`, `USUBJID`, `--SEQ`, `APID`, `POOLID`, `SPDEVID`

**Source:** [model/01_concepts_and_terms.md] — "Identifier variables — identify the study, subject, domain, and sequence number of the record"

---

### 2. Topic Variables

**Purpose:** Specify the focus of the observation — what the observation is about.

**Key characteristics:**
- Define the primary subject matter of the record
- Follow Identifier variables in the variable ordering
- The specific topic variable differs by observation class:
  - **Interventions:** `--TRT` (e.g., `CMTRT`, `EXTRT`) — the treatment name
  - **Events:** `--TERM` (e.g., `AETERM`, `MHTERM`) — the event term
  - **Findings:** `--TESTCD` / `--TEST` (e.g., `LBTESTCD`, `VSTESTCD`) — the measurement/test name
- In relationship datasets (SUPPQUAL), `QNAM` serves as the Topic variable

**Source:** [model/01_concepts_and_terms.md] — "Topic variables — specify the focus of the observation (e.g., the name of a lab test)"

---

### 3. Qualifier Variables

**Purpose:** Include additional illustrative text or numeric values that describe the results or additional traits of the observation.

**Key characteristics:**
- The largest and most diverse role category
- Follow Topic variables in the variable ordering
- Divided into **5 subclasses**:

| Subclass | Purpose | Examples |
|----------|---------|----------|
| **Grouping Qualifiers** | Group observations within the same domain | `--CAT`, `--SCAT` |
| **Result Qualifiers** | Describe specific results (Findings only) | `--ORRES`, `--STRESC`, `--STRESN` |
| **Synonym Qualifiers** | Specify alternative names for a variable | `--MODIFY`, `--DECOD` (for `--TRT`/`--TERM`); `--TEST` (for `--TESTCD`) |
| **Record Qualifiers** | Define additional attributes of the entire observation record | `--REASND`, `AESLIFE`, `AGE`, `SEX`, `--BLFL`, `--POS`, `--LOC`, `--SPEC` |
| **Variable Qualifiers** | Modify or describe a specific variable within an observation | `--ORRESU` (qualifies `--ORRES`), `--DOSU` (qualifies `--DOSE`) |

**Source:** [chapters/ch02_fundamentals.md] — Qualifier Variable Subclasses table

---

### Summary Comparison Table

| Aspect | Identifier | Topic | Qualifier |
|--------|-----------|-------|-----------|
| **Primary function** | Identify record context | Define observation focus | Describe/qualify the observation |
| **Order in dataset** | First | Second | Third (before Timing) |
| **Examples** | `STUDYID`, `USUBJID`, `--SEQ` | `CMTRT`, `AETERM`, `LBTESTCD` | `--CAT`, `--ORRES`, `--SEV`, `--DECOD` |
| **Cross-domain linkage** | Yes (primary keys) | No (domain-specific) | Sometimes (e.g., `--DECOD` via MedDRA) |
| **Role in SUPPQUAL** | `STUDYID`, `RDOMAIN`, `USUBJID`, `IDVAR`, `IDVARVAL` | `QNAM` | `QLABEL` (Synonym), `QVAL` (Result), `QORIG`/`QEVAL` (Record) |

**Source:** [model/01_concepts_and_terms.md] — Variable Roles section; [chapters/ch02_fundamentals.md] — §2.1 Observations and Variables

---

### Variable Ordering Rule

For the 3 general observation classes (Interventions, Events, Findings), variables **must be ordered** as: **Identifiers first, followed by Topic, Qualifier, and Timing variables**. Within each role, variables must follow the order shown in the SDTM model sections.

**Source:** [chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md] — §4.1.4 Order of the Variables

Based on the retrieved context, a sponsor should follow these steps to create a new custom domain in SDTM:

1. **Determine the General Observation Class**: First, determine whether the observation represents an **Intervention**, **Event**, or **Finding** by considering the content of the information in light of the definitions of the 3 general observation classes, rather than by trying to deduce the class from the information's physical structure. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md]**

Any letter or number may be used in the second position. Note that the use of codes beginning with X, Y, or Z is optional and not required for custom domains. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md]**

The 2-character domain code is limited to A-Z for the first character, and A-Z, 0-9 for the second character. No other characters are allowed. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md]**

4. **Follow the General Observation Class Model**: The domain models in Section 6 of the SDTMIG illustrate how to apply the SDTM when creating a specific domain dataset, including selecting a subset of variables offered in one of the general observation classes along with applicable timing variables. These models show how to adjust standard variables to meet specific content needs. **[Source: chapters/ch03_submitting_data.md]**

5. **Document in Define-XML**: The Define-XML document that accompanies a submission should describe each dataset, including dataset filenames, descriptions, locations, structures, class, purpose, and keys. **[Source: chapters/ch03_submitting_data.md]**

## SDTM Core Designations and Permissible Variable Rules

### Three Core Designation Categories

The SDTM specifies three Core designation categories for variables:

| Core Value | Meaning | Rule |
|------------|---------|------|
| **Req** (Required) | A Required variable is any variable that is basic to the identification of a data record (i.e., essential key variables and a topic variable) or is necessary to make the record meaningful. | Must always be included in the dataset and **cannot be null for any record**. |
| **Exp** (Expected) | Must be included in the dataset. | Value should be populated when available; null values allowed when data not collected/applicable; must still include the column and add a comment in the Define-XML document to state that the study does not include the data item. |
| **Perm** (Permissible) | May be included in the dataset. | Rules depend on whether the data item was collected (see below). |

**[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]**

### Rules for Permissible Variables When a Study Did Not Collect the Data Item

When a study **did not include** a data item that would be represented in a Permissible variable:

> **That variable should NOT be included in the SDTM dataset and should NOT be declared in the Define-XML document.**

**[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]**

### Contrast: When a Study DID Collect the Data Item

For completeness, if a study **did include** a data item that would be represented in a Permissible variable:

> **That variable MUST be included in the SDTM dataset, even if null. Indicate no data were available for that variable in the Define-XML document.**

**[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]**

### Additional Note on Permissible Variables

Although domain specification tables list only some of the identifier, timing, and general observation class variables, **all are permissible** unless specifically restricted in the implementation guide or by specific domain assumptions. Domain assumptions that say a Permissible variable is "generally not used" do not prohibit use of the variable.

**[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]**
