results.answer:
Based on the retrieved context, the definitions of an intervention versus an event are as follows:

**Intervention:** An intervention is something that is done to a subject (possibly by the subject) that is expected to have a physiological effect. This concept of intended effect makes interventions relatively easy to recognize, although there are gray areas around some testing procedures (e.g., exercise stress tests are designed to produce and then measure certain physiological effects; the measurements from such a testing procedure are findings, although some aspects of the procedure might be modeled as interventions). **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.1]**

**Event:** An event is something that happens to a subject spontaneously. Most, although not all, events data captured in clinical trials is about medical events. Because many medical events must, by regulation, be treated as adverse events, a new Events domain will be created only for events that are clearly not adverse events; the existing Medical History (MH) and Clinical Events (CE) domains are the appropriate places to store most medical events that are not adverse events. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.1]**

**Key Differentiating Factors:**
- Interventions are **done to** a subject with an **expected physiological effect**.
- Events **happen to** a subject **spontaneously**.
- The structure of the data can also help: log forms (completed over the course of the study) suggest Events or Interventions, while observations made at individual visits are usually planned Findings. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.3]**
- If verbatim text is collected and then coded, this suggests Events or Interventions class data (where the topic variable is coded), whereas for Findings class data, the result is coded. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md -- 8.6.3]**

results.answer:
## Associated Persons in SDTM

**Associated Persons** are individuals other than study subjects who can be associated with a study, a particular study subject, or a device used in the study. The structures of SDTM datasets that represent data about associated persons are based on the structures for data about study subjects, using either general observation class structures or special-purpose domain structures. **[Source: model/04_associated_persons.md]**

### Key Characteristics

- AP domains conform to the same general observation class models (Interventions, Events, Findings) used for subject data
- The same variables, roles, and controlled terminology apply
- AP domains use the variable **APID** (Associated Persons Identifier) instead of USUBJID for subjects
- Linking variables include **RSUBJID** (Related Subject or Pool Identifier), **RDEVID** (Related Device Identifier), and **SREL** (Subject, Device, or Study Relationship)
- AP domains are not part of the core SDTMIG for human clinical trials; additional guidance is provided in the SDTM Implementation Guide: Associated Persons (SDTMIG-AP) **[Source: model/04_associated_persons.md]**

## AP Domain Naming Convention

AP domains use the domain code prefix `AP` followed by the relevant domain code. For example, associated persons demographics would use `APDM`. **[Source: model/04_associated_persons.md]**

### Relationship to Standard Domain Codes

Standard SDTM domain codes are defined in the **SDTM Domain Abbreviation codelist (C66734)**. **[Source: domains/RELREC/spec.md; chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md]**

The standard 2-character domain code convention (limited to A-Z for the first character, and A-Z, 0-9 for the second character) applies, with AP domains extending this by prepending "AP" to create a 4-character prefix. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md]**

### Dataset Naming Exceptions

When supplemental qualifiers are needed for AP domains, the dataset name with the "SUPP" fragment (e.g., SUPPAPFAMH) would be too long. In this case only, the "SUPP" portion should be shortened to "SQ" (e.g., resulting in the dataset name SQAPFAMH). **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md]**

### Associated Persons Relationships Dataset

## Expected (Exp) Core Variable in SDTM

An **Expected (Exp)** variable is a variable that is necessary to make a record useful in the context of a specific domain. Expected variables may contain some null values, but in most cases will not contain null values for every record.

### Definition from SDTMIG v3.4

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Label** | Expected |
| **Meaning** | Must be included in the dataset |
| **Rule** | Value should be populated when available; null values allowed when data not collected/applicable |

**[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]**

### Requirements When a Study Does Not Collect the Data Item

When the study does not include the data item for an Expected variable, the following must be done:

1. **A null column must still be included in the dataset** — the variable column must be present even though all values will be null.
2. **A comment must be included in the Define-XML document** — the Define-XML must state that the study does not include the data item.

**[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]**

### Comparison with Other Core Designations

| Core Value | Included in Dataset? | Null Values Allowed? | Define-XML Comment Required? |
|------------|---------------------|---------------------|------------------------------|
| **Req** (Required) | Always | No — cannot be null for any record | N/A |
| **Exp** (Expected) | Always | Yes — when data not collected/applicable | Yes — must state data item not collected |
| **Perm** (Permissible) | Only if data collected | Yes — if included | Yes — if included and null |

**[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]**

### Key Distinction

The critical difference between Expected and Permissible variables when data are not collected:
- **Expected**: The column **must** be included in the dataset (with all null values) and declared in Define-XML with a comment explaining the data were not collected.
- **Permissible**: If the study did not collect the data, the variable **should not** be included in the dataset and **should not** be declared in Define-XML.

**[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]**

results.answer:
## SDTM Decision: Supplemental Qualifiers vs. Findings About (FA) Domain

The decision between storing assessments of an event as Supplemental Qualifiers (SUPP--) versus in the Findings About (FA) domain is governed by **three criteria** defined in the SDTMIG. The key distinction is whether the assessment applies to the **event as a whole** or to a **part/snapshot** of the event with different timing.

---

### Criterion 1: Timing — Does the assessment have different timing from the event as a whole?

| Scenario | Placement | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|-----------|
| Assessment applies to the **entire event** (e.g., overall severity of an AE) | **Supplemental Qualifier** (or built-in qualifier like --SEV, --TOXGR) | The assessment shares the event's timing; no separate temporal dimension needed |
| Assessment is a **snapshot/slice** of the event at a specific time point (e.g., severity of a symptom measured at multiple visits) | **FA domain** | The assessment has its own timing, different from the event's start/end dates |

**Source:** [domains/FA/assumptions.md — item_6] — "A finding that is about part of an event, rather than the event as a whole, meets this criterion for the use of FA."

---

### Criterion 2: Complexity — Does the assessment require more than 1 variable for its representation?

| Scenario | Placement | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|-----------|
| Assessment can be represented by a **single variable** (e.g., a single flag or text value) | **Supplemental Qualifier** | SUPP-- is designed for single non-standard variable/value combinations |
| Assessment requires **2 or more variables** (e.g., a test code + result + units + reference range) | **FA domain** | FA provides the full Findings structure (--TESTCD, --TEST, --ORRES, --ORRESU, etc.) |

**Source:** [domains/FA/assumptions.md — item_6] — "The need to represent data which require more than 1 variable in a findings about structure, rather than by adding 2 or more supplemental qualifiers to the parent record, is the basis for this criterion."

---

### Criterion 3: Pre-specified AE Occurrence — Does the data indicate occurrence of pre-specified AEs?

| Scenario | Placement | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|-----------|
| Data indicate whether a **pre-specified AE occurred** (e.g., a checklist of expected events) | **FA domain** | This criterion was specifically added to replace the old "no parent record exists" criterion |
| Data are a **subjective attribution** by an evaluator (e.g., "treatment-emergent" flag) | **Supplemental Qualifier** | Attributions are explicitly handled by SUPP-- with QEVAL populated |

**Source:** [domains/FA/assumptions.md — item_6] — "Data or information that indicate the occurrence of pre-specified AEs" is Criterion 3 for FA.

---

### Additional Decision Rules

#### 1. Built-in Qualifiers Stay in the Parent Domain
Some assessments of events have been **built into the SDTM Events model as qualifiers** (e.g., --SEV, --TOXGR, --REASND). These are **not** moved to FA or SUPP--; they remain as standard variables in the Events domain.

**Source:** [chapters/ch08_relationships.md — §8.6.3] — "Some assessments of events (e.g., severity, relationship to study treatment) have been built into the SDTM Events model as qualifiers, rather than being treated as findings about events."

#### 2. When FA is Used, FATESTCD Mirrors the Variable Name
When FA is used to represent findings about a **part** of the event, the FATEST and FATESTCD values should be the same as the variable name and variable label in the corresponding event or intervention domain (e.g., FATESTCD = "OCCUR", "SEV", "TOXGR").

**Source:** [domains/FA/assumptions.md — item_4] — "When FA is used to represent findings about a part of the event or intervention... the FATEST and FATESTCD values should be the same as the variable name and variable label in the corresponding event or intervention domain."

#### 3. SUPP-- is for Single Non-standard Variables
SUPP-- is specifically designed for **non-standard variables (NSVs)** that cannot be accommodated by the standard SDTM model. Each SUPP-- record represents one NSV/value combination. Data that represent **separate observations** should be treated as separate observations (i.e., in FA), not as supplemental qualifiers.

**Source:** [domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md — overview] — "Data that represent separate observations should be treated as separate observations."

#### 4. Multiple Attributions Use Separate QNAM Values
If multiple evaluators provide the same type of assessment (e.g., treatment-emergent determination by investigator and adjudicator), separate QNAM values should be used (e.g., "AETRTEMI", "AETRTEMA") rather than creating multiple records with the same QNAM.

**Source:** [domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md — overview] — "If 2 individuals... provide a determination regarding whether an adverse event is treatment-emergent, then separate QNAM values should be used for each set of information."

---

### Decision Flowchart

```
Is the assessment about the event as a whole?
├── YES → Is it a built-in qualifier (--SEV, --TOXGR, etc.)?
│   ├── YES → Keep in parent Events domain
│   └── NO → Can it be represented by a single variable?
│       ├── YES → Supplemental Qualifier (SUPP--)
│       └── NO → FA domain
└── NO (assessment has different timing from the event) → FA domain
```

---

### Summary Table

| Decision Factor | Supplemental Qualifier (SUPP--) | Findings About (FA) |
|----------------|-------------------------------|---------------------|
| **Timing** | Same as parent event | Different timing from parent event |
| **Variables needed** | 1 variable (QNAM + QVAL) | 2+ variables (--TESTCD, --TEST, --ORRES, etc.) |
| **Nature** | Attribution, flag, or single qualifier | Measurement, test result, or multi-variable observation |
| **Evaluator** | QEVAL populated for subjective attributions | --EVAL variable in FA |
| **Example** | "Treatment-emergent" flag (AETRTEMI) | Severity of headache at each post-dose time point |
| **Parent record required** | Yes (linked via IDVAR/IDVARVAL) | May or may not have a parent record |

**Sources:** [domains/FA/assumptions.md — item_6], [chapters/ch08_relationships.md — §8.6.3], [domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md — overview], [domains/FA/assumptions.md — item_4]

Based on the retrieved context, the key distinction between **ETCD**, **TSPARMCD**, and **ARMCD** compared to **--TESTCD** lies in their character restrictions and maximum lengths.

### Summary of Differences

| Variable | Maximum Length | Character Restrictions (no numbers at start, no special chars) |
|----------|----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| **--TESTCD** | 8 characters | **Yes** — Cannot start with a number; cannot contain characters other than letters, numbers, or underscores. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.2.1]** |
| **ETCD** | 8 characters | **No** — Does not have the special character restrictions that apply to --TESTCD. **[Source: domains/TE/spec.md; domains/SE/spec.md; domains/TA/spec.md]** |
| **TSPARMCD** | 8 characters | **No** — Does not have the special character restrictions that apply to --TESTCD. **[Source: domains/TS/spec.md]** |
| **ARMCD** | 20 characters | **No** — Does not have the special character restrictions that apply to --TESTCD. **[Source: domains/DM/spec.md; domains/TA/spec.md; domains/TV/spec.md; chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.2.1]** |

### Detailed Explanation

1.  **--TESTCD (Findings)**: This variable is subject to the strictest rules. It is limited to **8 characters** and **cannot start with a number**, nor can it contain characters other than letters, numbers, or underscores. This is to ensure compatibility with SAS v5 transport files, as --TESTCD values may need to serve as variable names. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.2.1]**

2.  **ETCD (Element Code)**: Like --TESTCD, ETCD is limited to **8 characters** for ease of use in programming. However, it is **not subject to the same character restrictions** (e.g., it can start with a number or contain special characters) because it is not expected to serve as a variable name. **[Source: domains/TE/spec.md; domains/SE/spec.md; domains/TA/spec.md]**

3.  **TSPARMCD (Trial Summary Parameter Short Name)**: Similar to ETCD, TSPARMCD is limited to **8 characters** and does **not have special character restrictions**. It is designed to be short for programming convenience but is not expected to serve as a variable name. **[Source: domains/TS/spec.md]**

4.  **ARMCD (Planned Arm Code)**: ARMCD has a longer maximum length of **20 characters** to accommodate complex values needed for crossover trials (e.g., "AA-BB-CC-DD"). It is **not subject to the character restrictions** that apply to --TESTCD. The same rule applies to the companion variable ACTARMCD. **[Source: domains/DM/spec.md; domains/TA/spec.md; domains/TV/spec.md; chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.2.1]**

In summary, while --TESTCD is constrained by both length (8) and character set restrictions for potential use as a column name, ETCD and TSPARMCD share the 8-character length but are free from character restrictions, and ARMCD is given a longer 20-character limit with no character restrictions.

results.answer:
# Relative Timing Variables in SDTM

The SDTM model defines a set of **Relative Timing Variables** that describe the timing of an observation relative to a reference point or period. These are part of the Timing Variables for All Classes (48 variables total) and are available for use in any domain based on the 3 general observation classes (Interventions, Events, Findings), except where restricted by domain-specific assumptions.

## Variable Definitions

### Relative to the Sponsor-Defined Reference Period (--STRF, --ENRF)

These variables describe timing relative to the **continuous sponsor-defined study reference period**, which is bounded by RFSTDTC (start) and RFENDTC (end) in the Demographics (DM) dataset.

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core | Controlled Terms (C66728) |
|----------|-------|------|------|------|--------------------------|
| **--STRF** | Start Relative to Reference Period | Char | Timing | Perm | BEFORE, DURING, DURING/AFTER, AFTER, UNKNOWN |
| **--ENRF** | End Relative to Reference Period | Char | Timing | Perm | BEFORE, DURING, DURING/AFTER, AFTER, UNKNOWN |

**Source:** [model/02_observation_classes.md] — Timing Variables for All Classes, items 33-34

**Important restrictions:**
- Although "COINCIDENT" and "ONGOING" are in the STENRF codelist (C66728), they describe timing relative to a **point in time** rather than an interval, so they are **not appropriate** for use with --ENRF variables.
- These variables should be used when information such as "BEFORE", "PRIOR", "ONGOING", or "CONTINUING" is collected **in lieu of a date**, and this collected information is in relation to the sponsor-defined study reference period.

**Source:** [chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.4.7]

### Relative to a Specific Reference Time Point (--STRTPT, --STTPT, --ENRTPT, --ENTPT)

These variables are used when relative timing assessments are collected at times other than the start/end of the study reference period. They may be anchored with any timing description or date/time value.

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core | Controlled Terms (C66728) |
|----------|-------|------|------|------|--------------------------|
| **--STRTPT** | Start Relative to Reference Time Point | Char | Timing | Perm | BEFORE, COINCIDENT, AFTER, UNKNOWN |
| **--STTPT** | Reference Time Point for Start | Char | Timing | Perm | (free text) |
| **--ENRTPT** | End Relative to Reference Time Point | Char | Timing | Perm | BEFORE, COINCIDENT, AFTER, ONGOING, UNKNOWN |
| **--ENTPT** | Reference Time Point for End | Char | Timing | Perm | (free text) |

**Source:** [model/02_observation_classes.md] — Timing Variables for All Classes, items 37-40

**Important restrictions:**
- "DURING" and "DURING/AFTER" are in the STENRF codelist but describe timing relative to an **interval** of time, so are **not allowable** for use with --STRTPT and --ENRTPT variables.
- If the reference time point corresponds to the date of collection or assessment, **AFTER is not a valid value** for --STRTPT (it would represent an event after the date of collection).

**Source:** [chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.4.7]

## Allowable Values Summary

| Variable | Allowable Values | Reference Type |
|----------|-----------------|----------------|
| --STRF | BEFORE, DURING, DURING/AFTER, AFTER, UNKNOWN | Interval (study reference period) |
| --ENRF | BEFORE, DURING, DURING/AFTER, AFTER, UNKNOWN | Interval (study reference period) |
| --STRTPT | BEFORE, COINCIDENT, AFTER, UNKNOWN | Point in time |
| --ENRTPT | BEFORE, COINCIDENT, AFTER, ONGOING, UNKNOWN | Point in time |
| --STTPT | Free text | Description of reference point |
| --ENTPT | Free text | Description of reference point |

**Source:** [chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.4.7]

## Domain-Specific Usage Examples

### Adverse Events (AE)
- **AEENRF** may be used when "Ongoing" is assessed coincident with the end of the study reference period (RFENDTC)
- **AEENRTPT** with **AEENTPT** may be used when "Ongoing" is relative to another date (e.g., final safety follow-up visit date)

**Source:** [domains/AE/assumptions.md item_5]

### Medical History (MH)
- **MHENRF** may be used when "Ongoing" or "Active" is assessed coincident with the start of the study reference period (RFSTDTC)
- **MHENRTPT** and **MHENTPT** may be used when "Ongoing" is relative to another date (e.g., screening visit date)

**Source:** [domains/MH/assumptions.md item_5]

### Clinical Events (CE)
- **CESTRF** or **CEENRF** may be used when timing assessment is relative to the study reference period
- **CESTRTPT** with **CESTTPT** and/or **CEENRTPT** with **CEENTPT** may be used when "Prior" or "Ongoing" are relative to specific dates other than the start/end of the study reference period

**Source:** [domains/CE/assumptions.md item_5]

### Concomitant Medications (CM)
- **CMSTRF** = "BEFORE" when a CRF checkbox identifies medication use that began prior to the study reference period
- **CMENRF** = "DURING" when medication continues during the study reference period

**Source:** [chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.4.7]

## Controlled Terminology

All four relative timing variables (--STRF, --ENRF, --STRTPT, --ENRTPT) reference the same codelist: **C66728** (STENRF). However, not all values of this codelist are allowable for each variable — the specific restrictions are documented in Section 4.4.7 of the SDTMIG.

**Source:** [domains/SU/spec.md — SUSTRTPT], [domains/RS/spec.md — RSSTRTPT], [domains/CM/spec.md — CMSTRTPT], [domains/AE/spec.md — AEENRF]

## Caution on Derived Values

Sponsors are cautioned that deriving --STRF and --ENRF for analysis or reporting purposes even when dates are collected may blur the distinction between collected and derived values within the domain. Sponsors wishing to do such derivations are instead encouraged to use analysis datasets for this derived data.

**Source:** [chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.4.7]

results.answer:
Based on the retrieved context, here is how the LB domain distinguishes original from standardized results, the codelist for LBSTRESC, and its standard values.

### 1. Distinction between LBORRES and LBSTRESC

The LB domain uses a three-level result framework to separate the originally collected value from its standardized representation:

- **LBORRES (Result or Finding in Original Units):** This variable always contains the value exactly as originally collected or reported from the source. It is the "raw" data. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.5.1]**
- **LBSTRESC (Character Result/Finding in Std Format):** This variable contains the result value copied or derived from LBORRES, but converted into a standard format or standard units. It must be populated whenever LBORRES is populated. **[Source: domains/LB/spec.md — LBSTRESC]**
- **LBSTRESN (Numeric Result/Finding in Standard Units):** This is the numeric version of LBSTRESC, populated only for continuous or numeric results. **[Source: domains/LB/spec.md — LBSTRESN]**

**Example:** If a pregnancy test result is collected as "-" (a minus sign) in LBORRES, it is standardized to the text value "NEGATIVE" in LBSTRESC. **[Source: domains/LB/examples.md — Example 3, Row 1]**

### 2. Codelist for LBSTRESC

LBSTRESC references the **Laboratory Test Standard Character Result (C102580)** codelist. **[Source: domains/LB/spec.md — LBSTRESC; domains/LB/spec.md — Controlled Terminology]**

This codelist is **Extensible**, meaning additional values beyond those listed can be used. **[Source: terminology/core/lb_part4.md]**

### 3. Standard Result Values for Positive/Negative Findings

The codelist C102580 includes the following standard values relevant to positive/negative findings:

| CDISC Submission Value | CDISC Definition |
|------------------------|------------------|
| NEGATIVE | A finding of normality following an examination or investigation looking for the presence of a microorganism, disease, or condition. |
| POSITIVE | An observation confirming something, such as the presence of a disease, condition, or microorganism. |
| BORDERLINE | Straddling the dividing line between two categories. |
| INDETERMINATE | Cannot distinguish between two or more possible values in the current context. |
| INVALID | Not valid data. |
| TRACE | A barely detectable amount. |

**[Source: terminology/core/lb_part4.md]**

**Note:** Per Rule 7, the individual value codes (e.g., C38757 for NEGATIVE) are not provided here because the retrieved context only shows the value names and definitions, not the per-value NCI codes. The codelist code C102580 is confirmed from the source.

Based on the retrieved context, the variable **FOCID** is defined in the **OE (Ophthalmic Examinations)** domain and is also referenced for use in other subject-level domains.

### Definition of FOCID

- **Label:** Focus of Study-Specific Interest
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Identifier
- **Core:** Perm (Permissible)
- **Controlled Terms:** C119013 (Ophthalmic Focus of Study Specific Interest codelist)
- **CDISC Notes:** Identification of a focus of study-specific interest on or within a subject or specimen as called out in the protocol for which a measurement, test, or examination was performed. **[Source: domains/OE/spec.md]**

### Domains Where FOCID is Defined

1.  **OE (Ophthalmic Examinations):** FOCID is explicitly defined in the OE domain specification with a controlled terminology codelist (C119013). **[Source: domains/OE/spec.md]**
2.  **MB (Microbiology Specimen):** FOCID is defined as a Permissible variable in the MB domain specification. **[Source: domains/MB/spec.md]**
3.  **NV (Nervous System Findings):** FOCID is defined as a Permissible variable in the NV domain specification. **[Source: domains/NV/spec.md]**

### Usage in Ophthalmology Data

In ophthalmic studies, the eyes are usually sites of treatment. It is appropriate to identify sites using the variable FOCID. When FOCID is used to identify the eyes, it is recommended that the values "OD" (oculus dexter, right eye), "OS" (oculus sinister, left eye), and "OU" (oculus uterque, both eyes) be used in FOCID. These terms are the exclusively preferred terms used by the ophthalmology community as abbreviations for the expanded Latin terms, and are included in the nonextensible CDISC Ophthalmic Focus of Study Specific Interest (OEFOCUS) codelist. **[Source: domains/OE/assumptions.md]**

### Broader Application

In any study that uses FOCID, FOCID would be included in records in any subject-level domain representing findings, interventions, or events (e.g., Adverse Events) related to the eyes. **[Source: domains/OE/assumptions.md]**

The value in this variable should have inherent semantic meaning, such as a drug application site (e.g., "Injection site 1", "Biopsy site 1", "Treated site 1") or a more specific focus (e.g., "OD" (right eye), "Upper left quadrant of the back"). **[Source: domains/NV/spec.md]**

### Controlled Terminology (C119013)

The Ophthalmic Focus of Study Specific Interest codelist (C119013) is nonextensible and contains the following values:

| Code | CDISC Submission Value | Definition |
|------|----------------------|------------|
| C119333 | OD | The eye positioned in the right orbit, Oculus Dexter. |
| C119334 | OS | The eye positioned in the left orbit, Oculus Sinister. |
| C119335 | OU | Of or pertaining to both the left and right eyes, Oculus Uterque. |

**[Source: terminology/core/other_part2.md]**

### Summary

FOCID captures the specific anatomical focus or site of interest within a study (e.g., right eye, left eye, injection site). It is defined in the OE, MB, and NV domain specifications but can be used across any subject-level domain (Findings, Interventions, or Events) when data relate to a specific focus of study interest. For ophthalmology data, the recommended values are "OD", "OS", and "OU" from the C119013 codelist.

results.answer:
## Answer

When building a supplemental qualifier dataset for the Demographics (DM) domain, **both IDVAR and IDVARVAL must be null (empty)** for every record.

### Why This Differs from Other Domains

The reason is that DM has a **one-to-one relationship with USUBJID** — there is exactly one record per subject in DM. Therefore, the combination of `STUDYID`, `RDOMAIN`, and `USUBJID` is already sufficient to uniquely identify the parent record. No additional identifying variable is needed.

For all other parent domains (general-observation class datasets like AE, LB, VS, etc.), the parent dataset may have multiple records per subject, so `IDVAR` and `IDVARVAL` are required to pinpoint which specific parent record the supplemental qualifier belongs to.

### Key Rules

| Variable | DM (Special Case) | Other Domains |
|----------|-------------------|---------------|
| IDVAR | Null | Populated (e.g., `AESEQ`, `LBSEQ`, `--GRPID`) |
| IDVARVAL | Null | Populated with the value of the identifying variable |

### Source Citations

- **"An exception is SUPP-- dataset records that are related to Demographics (DM) records, where both IDVAR and IDVARVAL will be null because the key variables STUDYID, RDOMAIN, and USUBJID are sufficient to identify the unique parent record in DM (DM has 1 record per USUBJID)."**  
  **[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md]**

- **"A record in a SUPP-- dataset relates back to its parent record(s) via the key identified by the STUDYID, RDOMAIN, USUBJID, and IDVAR/IDVARVAL variables. An exception is SUPP-- dataset records that are related to Demographics (DM) records, where both IDVAR and IDVARVAL will be null because STUDYID, RDOMAIN, and USUBJID are sufficient to identify the unique parent record in DM (DM has 1 record per USUBJID)."**  
  **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md — Key Rules]**

### Example: SUPPDM Structure

For a DM supplemental qualifier dataset (suppdm.xpt), the records would look like:

| STUDYID | RDOMAIN | USUBJID | IDVAR | IDVARVAL | QNAM | QLABEL | QVAL | QORIG | QEVAL |
|---------|---------|---------|-------|----------|------|--------|------|-------|-------|
| ABC123 | DM | SUBJ-001 | | | DMETHNIC | Ethnicity Detail | HISPANIC OR LATINO | CRF | |
| ABC123 | DM | SUBJ-002 | | | DMETHNIC | Ethnicity Detail | NOT HISPANIC OR LATINO | CRF | |

Note that `IDVAR` and `IDVARVAL` are null because `STUDYID` + `RDOMAIN` + `USUBJID` uniquely identifies the single DM record per subject.

results.answer:
Based on the retrieved context, here is how to populate RELREC for dataset-level relationships:

## RELTYPE

For dataset-to-dataset relationships, RELTYPE identifies the hierarchical level of the relationship. The allowable values are **ONE** and **MANY** (controlled terminology is expected, codelist C78737). The possible combinations are:

- **ONE and ONE**: No hierarchical relationship; only 1 record from each dataset will potentially have the same IDVAR value within USUBJID.
- **ONE and MANY**: A hierarchical (parent-child) relationship; 1 record in the "ONE" dataset may relate to many records in the "MANY" dataset.
- **MANY and MANY**: Unusual and challenging to manage; may represent a relationship never intended to convey a usable merge/join.

**[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md §8.3.1]**

## USUBJID and IDVARVAL

For dataset-level relationships, **both USUBJID and IDVARVAL must be null**. This is explicitly stated in the examples: "Note that because this is a dataset-to-dataset relationship, USUBJID and IDVARVAL are null."

**[Source: domains/RELREC/examples.md §Dataset Relationship Example; chapters/ch08_relationships.md §8.3.1]**

## Using --SEQ as the Join Key

**No, --SEQ cannot be used as IDVAR for dataset-level relationships.** The context states: "Because IDVAR identifies the keys that can be used to merge/join records between the datasets, --SEQ cannot be used. --SEQ only has meaning within a subject within a dataset, not across datasets."

Instead, variables such as **--GRPID, --SPID, --REFID, --LNKID, or --LNKGRP** are typically used as the merge key for dataset-level relationships.

**[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md §8.3.1]**

- **Purpose:** Indicates the **source** of the data value in QVAL — i.e., how the value was obtained. Examples: "CRF" (collected on a case report form), "Assigned", "Derived". **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md §8.4.1]**

QORIG is **always required** (Core: Req) for every SUPP-- record. **[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md — QORIG]**

### QEVAL — Evaluator

- **Label:** Evaluator
- **Type:** Char
- **Controlled Terms:** C78735
- **Role:** Record Qualifier
- **Core:** Exp (Expected)
- **Purpose:** Identifies the **person or group** who assigned the value in QVAL. Used only for **subjective** data (e.g., assigned by a person or committee). **[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/spec.md — QEVAL]**

### When QEVAL Should Be Left Blank

QEVAL should be **null** for records that contain **objectively collected or derived data**. Specifically:

1. **Objective data** (collected or derived algorithmically) → QEVAL = null. **[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md — overview]**
2. **Subjective data** (attributions where values are assigned by a person or committee) → QEVAL should reflect the role of the evaluator (e.g., "ADJUDICATION COMMITTEE", "SPONSOR", "INVESTIGATOR"). **[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md — overview]**

### Key Distinction

| Aspect | QORIG | QEVAL |
|--------|-------|-------|
| **What it describes** | How the data was obtained (source/method) | Who evaluated/assigned the value |
| **Core** | Req (always populated) | Exp (populated only for subjective data) |
| **Example values** | "CRF", "Derived", "Assigned" | "ADJUDICATION COMMITTEE", "SPONSOR", "INVESTIGATOR" |
| **Null allowed?** | No | Yes — for objective data |

**Example from context:** In the SUPPAE example, a treatment emergent flag with QORIG = "Derived" and QEVAL = "SPONSOR" indicates the value was derived algorithmically by the sponsor. A severity assessment with QORIG = "CRF" and QEVAL = "ADJUDICATION COMMITTEE" indicates the value was collected on a CRF and evaluated by an adjudication committee. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md §8.4.3, Example 1]**

### Summary

- **QORIG** = source/method of the data (always required)
- **QEVAL** = evaluator of subjective data (leave blank for objective/derived data)

results.answer:
## Answer

In the RELSPEC (Related Specimens) dataset, the distinction between an originally collected specimen and a derived aliquot is determined by the combination of the **PARENT** and **LEVEL** fields:

### Identifying Originally Collected vs. Derived Specimens

- **Originally collected specimen**: A row with `LEVEL = 1` **and** a blank/null value for `PARENT` indicates a collected (original) sample. **[Source: domains/RELSPEC/examples.md]**; **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md]**

- **Derived aliquot**: All other rows (where `LEVEL > 1` or `PARENT` is populated) represent a derived sample (e.g., aliquots, processed specimens). **[Source: domains/RELSPEC/examples.md]**; **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md]**

### What LEVEL Represents

The `LEVEL` variable identifies the **generation number** of the sample, where the collected sample is considered the **first generation** (Level 1). **[Source: domains/RELSPEC/spec.md]**

| Variable | Label | Type | Role | Core | CDISC Notes |
|----------|-------|------|------|------|-------------|
| LEVEL | Specimen Level | Num | Variable Qualifier | Req | Identifies the generation number of the sample where the collected sample is considered the first generation. **[Source: domains/RELSPEC/spec.md]** |

### Practical Interpretation

- **LEVEL = 1**: First generation (originally collected specimen)
- **LEVEL = 2**: Second generation (child/aliquot of a Level 1 specimen)
- **LEVEL = 3**: Third generation (child/aliquot of a Level 2 specimen)
- And so on...

### Example from the Knowledge Base

Using the specimen lineage example:

| REFID | SPEC | PARENT | LEVEL | Interpretation |
|-------|------|--------|-------|----------------|
| SPC-001 | TISSUE | (blank) | 1 | Originally collected specimen |
| SPC-001-A | TISSUE | SPC-001 | 2 | Derived aliquot (child of SPC-001) |
| SPC-001-B | TISSUE | SPC-001 | 2 | Derived aliquot (child of SPC-001) |
| SPC-001-B-1 | DNA | SPC-001-B | 3 | Derived aliquot (child of SPC-001-B) |
| SPC-003 | TISSUE | (blank) | 1 | Originally collected specimen |
| SPC-003-A | RNA | SPC-003 | 2 | Derived aliquot (child of SPC-003) |

**[Source: domains/RELSPEC/examples.md]**; **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md]**

### Key Rule

> "A specimen with a LEVEL value of '1' and a blank value for PARENT indicates a collected sample. All other values represent a derived sample." **[Source: domains/RELSPEC/examples.md]**; **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md]**

The `SPEC` variable reflects the specimen type for the sample regardless of whether it is collected or derived. **[Source: domains/RELSPEC/examples.md]**

results.answer:
Based on the retrieved context, you should store each evaluator's determination using **separate, unique QNAM values** in the SUPPAE dataset. This ensures that when the data are joined or transposed back to the parent AE record, no information is lost.

The key rule is stated in the SUPPQUAL assumptions:

> "If 2 individuals (e.g., the investigator and an independent adjudicator) provide a determination regarding whether an adverse event is treatment-emergent, then separate QNAM values should be used for each set of information (e.g., "AETRTEMI", "AETRTEMA"). This is necessary to ensure that reviewers can join/merge/transpose the information back with the records in the original domain without risk of losing information."

**[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md]**

The same guidance is reinforced in the general assumptions chapter:

> "For observations that have primary and secondary evaluations of specific qualifier variables, sponsors should put data from the primary evaluation into the standard domain dataset and data from the secondary evaluation into the Supplemental Qualifier datasets (SUPP--). Within each SUPP-- record, the value for QNAM should be formed by appending a "1" to the corresponding standard domain variable name."

**[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.5.4]**

---

### Implementation

Following the naming convention from the examples, you would:

1. **Primary evaluation (investigator):** Store in the standard AE domain variable `AETRTEM` (Treatment Emergent Flag).
2. **Secondary evaluation (adjudicator):** Store in SUPPAE using a distinct QNAM, such as `AETRTEMA` (appending "A" for adjudicator).

**Example SUPPAE records:**

| STUDYID | RDOMAIN | USUBJID | IDVAR | IDVARVAL | QNAM | QLABEL | QVAL | QORIG | QEVAL |
|---------|---------|---------|-------|----------|------|--------|------|-------|-------|
| 1996001 | AE | 99-401 | AESEQ | 1 | AETRTEM | Treatment Emergent Flag | Y | CRF | INVESTIGATOR |
| 1996001 | AE | 99-401 | AESEQ | 1 | AETRTEMA | Treatment Emergent Flag (Adjudicator) | N | CRF | ADJUDICATION COMMITTEE |

This pattern is consistent with the example in the general assumptions chapter where `AERELNS1` is used for a secondary evaluation of "Relationship to Non-study Treatment" by an adjudication committee **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.5.4]**.

---

### Key Rules

- **Unique QNAM per evaluator:** The combined set of values for `STUDYID`, `RDOMAIN`, `USUBJID`, `IDVAR`, `IDVARVAL`, and `QNAM` must be unique for every record. **[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md]**
- **QEVAL identifies the evaluator:** For subjective data (attributions), the value in `QEVAL` should reflect the role of the person or institution assigning the value (e.g., "INVESTIGATOR", "ADJUDICATION COMMITTEE", "SPONSOR"). **[Source: domains/SUPPQUAL/assumptions.md]**
- **8-character limit:** If the standard variable name is already 8 characters, replace the last character with a "1" (incremented for each additional attribution). For example, `AERELNST` (8 chars) becomes `AERELNS1` for the secondary evaluation. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.5.4]**

By using separate QNAM values (e.g., `AETRTEM` for investigator, `AETRTEMA` for adjudicator), both determinations are preserved without risk of one overwriting the other.

## EPOCH Derivation Guidance by Observation Class

### Findings Class Domains

For Findings class domains, **EPOCH should be based on `--DTC`** (Date/Time of Collection). This is because `--DTC` represents the date/time of the test or, for tests performed on specimens, the date/time of specimen collection.

**[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.3.1]**

This is confirmed in individual domain specifications, e.g.:
- **LB (Laboratory Test Results)**: "Epoch associated with the start date/time of the observation, or the date/time of collection if start date/time is not collected." **[Source: domains/LB/spec.md — EPOCH]**
- **IE (Inclusion/Exclusion)**: "Epoch associated with the observation date/time of the inclusion/exclusion finding." **[Source: domains/IE/spec.md — EPOCH]**
- **CP (Cell Phenotype Findings)**, **PC (Pharmacokinetics Concentrations)**, **PP (Pharmacokinetics Parameters)**: All use the same CDISC Note: "Epoch associated with the start date/time of the observation, or the date/time of collection if start date/time is not collected." **[Source: domains/CP/spec.md — EPOCH; domains/PC/spec.md — EPOCH; domains/PP/spec.md — EPOCH]**

### Interventions and Events Class Domains

For Interventions and Events class domains, **EPOCH should be based on `--STDTC`** (Start Date/Time of Observation), since this represents the start of the intervention or event.

**[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.3.1]**

For example, in the **DS (Disposition)** domain: "EPOCH is based on DSSTDTC." **[Source: domains/DS/assumptions.md §4c]**

### Exception for Findings with Interval Specimen Collection

A possible exception exists for Findings where an interval specimen collection started in one epoch but ended in another. In such cases, `--ENDTC` might be a more appropriate basis for EPOCH assignment. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.3.1]**

### When EPOCH Cannot Be Determined

When an observation's epoch cannot be determined:

1. **Do not impute EPOCH values.** Instead, assign EPOCH values based on CRF instructions and structure where possible, even if date/time data was not collected with sufficient precision to permit assignment based on date/time data alone.

2. **If it is not possible to determine the epoch**, then **EPOCH should be null**.

3. **Methods for assigning EPOCH values** can be described in the Define-XML document.

**[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.3.1]**

### Pre-Study Observations

EPOCH is a study-design construct and is **not applicable to**:
- Interventions or events that started **before the subject's participation in a study**
- Findings performed **before participation in a study**

For such records, **EPOCH should be null**. Note that a subject's participation in a study includes screening, which generally occurs before the reference start date (RFSTDTC) in the Demographics (DM) domain. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md §4.1.3.1]**

### Summary Table

| Observation Class | Base Variable | Notes |
|-------------------|---------------|-------|
| **Findings** | `--DTC` | Date/time of collection; exception: `--ENDTC` for interval specimen collections spanning epochs |
| **Interventions** | `--STDTC` | Start date/time of the intervention |
| **Events** | `--STDTC` | Start date/time of the event (e.g., DSSTDTC for Disposition) |
| **Undetermined** | — | Set EPOCH to null; document method in Define-XML |
| **Pre-study** | — | Set EPOCH to null (not applicable to pre-participation observations) |

results.answer:
## --LNKID vs --LNKGRP: Purpose and Use in RELREC

### Variable Definitions

**--LNKID (Link ID)**
- **Label:** Link ID
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Identifier
- **Core:** Exp (Expected in TU, TR; Permissible in other domains)
- **CDISC Notes:** Identifier used to link identified tumor/lesion/location of interest to the assessment results (in TR domain) over the course of the study. **[Source: domains/TU/spec.md]**

**--LNKGRP (Link Group ID)**
- **Label:** Link Group ID
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Identifier
- **Core:** Permissible
- **CDISC Notes:** Identifier used to link a group of records in one domain to a group of records in another domain.

---

### Key Differences

| Aspect | --LNKID | --LNKGRP |
|--------|---------|----------|
| **Granularity** | Links individual records (one-to-one or one-to-many) | Links groups of records (many-to-many or many-to-one) |
| **Primary Use Case** | TU ↔ TR (tumor identification to tumor results) | TR ↔ RS (tumor results to response assessment) |
| **Typical RELREC IDVAR** | Used as the value in IDVAR for dataset-to-dataset links | Used as the value in IDVAR for dataset-to-dataset links |
| **Relationship Type** | Typically ONE-to-MANY (one tumor ID → many assessment records) | Typically MANY-to-ONE (many tumor results → one response assessment) |

---

### How They Work in RELREC

#### --LNKID: TU ↔ TR Link

The TU and TR domains are split because they contain different observation classes (Findings vs. Events/Findings). The --LNKID variable provides the key for a **dataset-to-dataset relationship** in RELREC:

> "TRLNKID is used to relate records in the TR domain to an identification record in TU domain. The organization of data across the TU and TR domains requires a RELREC relationship to link the related data rows. A dataset-to-dataset link would be the most appropriate linking mechanism." **[Source: domains/TR/assumptions.md, item 1]**

The RELREC records would look like:

| STUDYID | RDOMAIN | USUBJID | IDVAR | IDVARVAL | RELTYPE | RELID |
|---------|---------|---------|-------|----------|---------|-------|
| EFC1234 | TU | | TULNKID | | ONE | 1 |
| EFC1234 | TR | | TRLNKID | | MANY | 1 |

**[Source: domains/RELREC/examples.md, Example 1]**

Note that USUBJID and IDVARVAL are **null** for dataset-to-dataset relationships, and RELTYPE indicates the cardinality (ONE/MANY).

#### --LNKGRP: TR ↔ RS Link

The --LNKGRP variable links multiple tumor/lesion result records to a single response assessment record:

> "TRLNKGRP is used to relate records in the TR domain to a response assessment record in the RS domain. The organization of data across the TR and RS domains requires a RELREC relationship to link the related data rows. A dataset-to-dataset link would be the most appropriate linking mechanism." **[Source: domains/TR/assumptions.md, item 2]**

This is necessary because a response evaluation (e.g., RECIST 1.1) typically requires aggregating measurements from multiple target lesions, which are stored across multiple TR records.

---

### Practical Guidance

1. **Use --LNKID when:**
   - You need a one-to-one or one-to-many link between individual records in two domains
   - The link is between a parent identification record and its child assessment records (TU ↔ TR)
   - Each value uniquely identifies a single entity (e.g., a specific tumor/lesion)

2. **Use --LNKGRP when:**
   - You need to link a group of records in one domain to a single record in another domain
   - The link is between multiple assessment results and a summary/response record (TR ↔ RS)
   - Multiple records share the same group identifier to indicate they collectively contribute to a single assessment

3. **Both variables serve as IDVAR values in RELREC** for dataset-to-dataset relationships, where USUBJID and IDVARVAL are left null. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md, Section 8.3]**

4. **The --LNKID and --LNKGRP variables exist specifically because** --GRPID, --REFID, and --SPID may already be used for other purposes within the domain, so dedicated linking variables were created to avoid conflicts. **[Source: domains/TR/assumptions.md, items 1 and 2]**

results.answer:
Based on the retrieved context, here is how to handle groups of associated persons in AP datasets:

## Group Identification in the AP Dataset

When assessments are performed on a group of associated persons collectively, the group is identified using the **APID** variable.

**APID** (Associated Persons Identifier) is defined as:
- **Label:** Associated Persons Identifier
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Identifier
- **Core:** Required in AP domains

Per the model: *"APID may identify a single associated person, a group of associated persons, or a pool of associated persons."* **[Source: model/04_associated_persons.md]**

Therefore, you would populate APID with a single identifier value that represents the entire group (e.g., "CAREGIVER_GROUP_01") rather than individual identifiers.

## Documenting Group Membership

When APID identifies a pool/group of associated persons, **POOLDEF records must exist for each associated person** in that pool. **[Source: model/04_associated_persons.md]**

The **POOLDEF** dataset (Pool Definition) has the following structure **[Source: model/06_relationship_datasets.md]**:

| # | Variable | Label | Type | Role |
|---|----------|-------|------|------|
| 1 | STUDYID | Study Identifier | Char | Identifier |
| 2 | POOLID | Pool Identifier | Char | Identifier |
| 3 | USUBJID | Unique Subject Identifier | Char | Identifier |
| 4 | APID | Associated Persons Identifier | Char | Identifier |

**How it works:**
1. In the AP dataset, set `APID = "CAREGIVER_GROUP_01"` for all records representing the group-level assessment.
2. In the POOLDEF dataset, create one record per individual associated person in the group, each with:
   - `POOLID = "CAREGIVER_GROUP_01"` (matching the APID value)
   - `APID = <individual APID>` (the unique identifier for each person in the group)

This creates the linkage: the group-level APID in the AP dataset points to POOLDEF, which enumerates each individual member of that group.

## Key Principle

*"If APID identifies a pool, POOLDEF records must exist for each associated person."* **[Source: model/04_associated_persons.md]**

This ensures that while the assessment data is recorded at the group level (one row per group), the composition of the group is fully documented and traceable to each individual associated person.

Additionally, a final disposition record in **DS** should be created to document the subject's death as the reason for discontinuation. **[Source: domains/SS/assumptions.md -- item_1]**

results.answer:
## Division of Work Between TU and TR in Oncology RECIST Studies

The SDTMIG v3.4 specifies a **multi-domain approach** for representing oncology assessment data, dividing identification and measurement responsibilities across two Findings domains:

### TU (Tumor/Lesion Identification) — Identification Domain

TU is a **Findings** domain that represents data that **uniquely identifies** tumors, lesions, or locations of interest under study. **[Source: domains/TU/assumptions.md — overview]**

**What TU contains:**
- A unique tumor/lesion/location ID value (TULNKID)
- Anatomical location of the tumor (TULOC, TULAT, TUDIR, TUPORTOT)
- Method used to identify the tumor (TUMETHOD)
- Role of the individual identifying the tumor (TUEVAL)
- Timing information (TUDTC, TUDY)
- Classification of the tumor (TUORRES: TARGET, NON-TARGET, NEW)

**Key rule:** TU should contain only **1 record for each unique tumor/lesion/location of interest** per medical evaluator. The initial identification is done once, usually at baseline, and must **not be repeated for every visit**. **[Source: domains/TU/assumptions.md — item_1]**

Post-baseline records in TU are limited to:
- New tumors/lesions that emerge during the study
- Split tumors/lesions (when a tumor divides into distinct parts)
- Re-baseline scenarios (e.g., cross-over studies) **[Source: domains/TU/assumptions.md — item_1]**

### TR (Tumor/Lesion Results) — Measurement Domain

TR is a **Findings** domain that represents **quantitative measurements and/or qualitative assessments** of the tumors, lesions, or locations of interest identified in TU. **[Source: domains/TR/assumptions.md — overview]**

**What TR contains:**
- Measurements (e.g., DIAMETER, SUMDIAM, SUMNLNLD)
- Qualitative assessments (e.g., TUMSTATE = PRESENT/ABSENT)
- Method used for measurement (TRMETHOD)
- Role of the assessor (TREVAL)
- Timing information (TRDTC, TRDY)
- Result values (TRORRES, TRSTRESC, TRSTRESN)

### How They Link

The linking mechanism uses **--LNKID** variables:
- **TULNKID** in TU provides a unique code for each identified tumor/lesion
- **TRLNKID** in TR contains matching values to link assessment records back to their identification records **[Source: domains/TU/assumptions.md — item_2]**

A RELREC dataset relationship record can be created to formally describe this link:

| STUDYID | RDOMAIN | USUBJID | IDVAR | IDVARVAL | RELTYPE | RELID |
|---------|---------|---------|-------|----------|---------|-------|
| EFC1234 | TU | | TULNKID | | ONE | 1 |
| EFC1234 | TR | | TRLNKID | | MANY | 1 |

**[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md — 8.3.1 RELREC Dataset Relationship Example]**

This is a **dataset-to-dataset** relationship (USUBJID and IDVARVAL are null), with RELTYPE = "ONE" for TU and "MANY" for TR, indicating a **one-to-many** (parent-child) relationship: one identification record in TU can have many measurement records in TR.

### Preventing Duplicate Anatomical Location Storage

The anatomical location information is stored **only in TU**, not in TR. The SDTMIG explicitly states:

> "The TR domain does not include anatomical location information on each measurement/assessment record, because this would duplicate information represented in TU. The multi-domain approach to representing oncology assessment data was developed largely to reduce duplication of stored information." **[Source: domains/TR/assumptions.md — overview]**

This means:
- **TULOC, TULAT, TUDIR, TUPORTOT** — appear only in TU
- **TR** — contains only measurements/assessments, linked back to TU via TRLNKID

### Example Workflow

Using RECIST 1.1 criteria **[Source: domains/TU/examples.md — Example 2]**:

**TU (identification at screening):**
| TULNKID | TUTESTCD | TUTEST | TUORRES | TULOC | TULAT | TUMETHOD |
|---------|----------|--------|---------|-------|-------|----------|
| T01 | TUMIDENT | Tumor Identification | TARGET | LIVER | | CT SCAN |
| T02 | TUMIDENT | Tumor Identification | TARGET | KIDNEY | RIGHT | CT SCAN |
| NT01 | TUMIDENT | Tumor Identification | NON-TARGET | THYROID GLAND | RIGHT | CT SCAN |

**TR (measurements at screening and follow-up):**
| TRLNKID | TRTESTCD | TRTEST | TRORRES | TRSTRESN | TRSTRESU | VISIT |
|---------|----------|--------|---------|----------|----------|-------|
| T01 | DIAMETER | Diameter | 17 | 17 | mm | SCREEN |
| T01 | DIAMETER | Diameter | 0 | 0 | mm | WEEK 6 |
| T02 | DIAMETER | Diameter | 16 | 16 | mm | SCREEN |

**[Source: domains/TR/examples.md — Example 2]**

### Summary

| Aspect | TU | TR |
|--------|----|----|
| **Purpose** | Identification of tumors/lesions | Measurements/assessments |
| **Anatomical location** | Yes (TULOC, TULAT, etc.) | No (not duplicated) |
| **Record frequency** | Once per tumor (baseline + new/split) | Every assessment visit |
| **Key variable** | TULNKID | TRLNKID |
| **Relationship** | ONE (parent) | MANY (child) |

Based on the retrieved context, here is how cause-of-death details, disposition events, and the death flag from AE are handled in SDTM:

## 1. Cause-of-Death Details → DD Domain

The **Death Details (DD)** domain is the designated location for recording cause-of-death information and other circumstances surrounding the death.

- **Test-level variables:** `DDTESTCD` (e.g., `PRCDTH` for Primary Cause of Death, `SECDTH` for Secondary Cause of Death) and `DDTEST` (e.g., "Primary Cause of Death") identify the specific detail being recorded. **[Source: domains/DD/examples.md -- Example 1]**
- **Controlled Terminology:** `DDTESTCD` uses codelist C116108 (SDTM Death Diagnosis and Details Test Code), and `DDTEST` uses codelist C116107 (SDTM Death Diagnosis and Details Test Name). **[Source: terminology/core/other_part4.md]**
- **Multiple causes:** The DD domain can accommodate multiple causes of death (primary, secondary, and other designations). **[Source: domains/DD/assumptions.md -- item_1]**
- **Other details:** DD may also include location of death (`LOCDTH`), whether the death was witnessed (`DTHWIND`), autopsy indicator (`AUTOPIND`), and other related information. **[Source: terminology/core/other_part4.md]**

## 2. Disposition Event → DS Domain

The **Disposition (DS)** domain records the subject's end of study participation as a disposition event.

- **Death as disposition:** When a subject dies, a DS record is created with `DSDECOD = "DEATH"` and `DSCAT = "DISPOSITION EVENT"`. **[Source: domains/DS/examples.md -- Example 4]**
- **Date of death:** The date of the disposition event (death) is recorded in `DSSTDTC`. **[Source: domains/DS/examples.md -- Example 1, Row 14-16]**
- **Epoch:** The epoch in which the death occurred is recorded in `EPOCH`. **[Source: domains/DS/examples.md -- Example 4]**

## 3. Death Flag in AE → Do NOT Re-collate in DD

The DD domain is **not intended to collate data** that are already collected in standard variables in other domains. Specifically:

- **AE.AESDTH** (Results in Death) — indicates whether a serious adverse event resulted in death. **[Source: domains/AE/spec.md -- AESDTH]**
- **AE.AEOUT** (Outcome of Adverse Event) — may contain "FATAL" as an outcome. **[Source: domains/DD/assumptions.md -- item_2]**
- **DS.DSTERM** (Reported Term for the Disposition Event) — may contain the death-related term. **[Source: domains/DD/assumptions.md -- item_2]**

The DD assumptions explicitly state: *"The DD domain is not intended to collate data that are collected in standard variables in other domains, such as AE.AEOUT (Outcome of Adverse Event), AE.AESDTH (Results in Death) or DS.DSTERM (Reported Term for the Disposition Event)."* **[Source: domains/DD/assumptions.md -- item_2]**

## 4. Death Flag in DM → DTHFL

The **Demographics (DM)** domain also contains a death flag:

- **DM.DTHFL** (Subject Death Flag) — indicates the subject died. Should be "Y" or null. Should be populated even when the death date is unknown. **[Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- DTHFL]**
- **Controlled Terms:** C66742 (same codelist as AESDTH). **[Source: domains/DM/spec.md -- DTHFL]**

## 5. Linking Across Domains → RELREC

When the same death event is represented across multiple domains (AE, DS, DD), the relationship between these records is established using the **RELREC** (Related Records) domain. **[Source: domains/DD/examples.md -- Example 2; domains/DS/examples.md -- Example 4]**

Example from the context:
- AE record with `AESDTH = "Y"` and `AEOUT = "FATAL"`
- DS record with `DSDECOD = "DEATH"`
- DD record with `DDTESTCD = "PRCDTH"` (Primary Cause of Death)
- All linked via RELREC using `IDVAR`/`IDVARVAL` pairs (e.g., `AESEQ`, `DSSEQ`, `DDSEQ`) **[Source: domains/DD/examples.md -- Example 2]**

## Summary Table

| Information | Domain | Key Variables | Notes |
|-------------|--------|---------------|-------|
| Cause of death details | DD | `DDTESTCD`, `DDTEST`, `DDORRES`, `DDSTRESC` | Primary, secondary, location, etc. |
| Disposition event (death) | DS | `DSDECOD = "DEATH"`, `DSSTDTC` | End of study participation |
| Death flag from AE | AE | `AESDTH`, `AEOUT` | Do NOT re-collate in DD |
| Subject death flag | DM | `DTHFL`, `DTHDTC` | Must be populated when subject dies |
| Relationships | RELREC | `RDOMAIN`, `IDVAR`, `IDVARVAL` | Links AE, DS, DD records |

results.answer:
Based on the retrieved context, the decision of whether a disease sign or symptom (such as a migraine episode) belongs in the Clinical Events (CE) domain versus the Adverse Events (AE) domain depends on the protocol's definition and regulatory consultation.

Here is the guidance from the SDTMIG v3.4:

1.  **Protocol Definition is Primary:** The determination of which events are considered clinical events versus adverse events should be made carefully, with reference to regulatory guidelines or consultation with a regulatory review division. Events of clinical interest as defined by the protocol that are **not** considered AEs should be reflected as CEs. **[Source: domains/CE/assumptions.md]**

2.  **Scope of AE Domain:** The AE dataset includes clinical data describing "any untoward medical occurrence in a patient or clinical investigation subject administered a pharmaceutical product." Sponsors may extend or limit the scope of AE collection (e.g., not collecting events assessed as efficacy endpoints). The events included in the AE dataset should be consistent with the protocol requirements. **[Source: domains/AE/assumptions.md]**

3.  **Examples of CE Use Cases:**
    - **Efficacy Endpoints:** In a study of an investigational treatment for prevention of ischemic stroke, all occurrences of TIA, stroke, and death might be captured as clinical events and assessed as to whether they meet endpoint criteria. **[Source: domains/CE/assumptions.md]**
    - **Non-AE Signs/Symptoms:** In a study of an investigational treatment for migraine headaches, migraine headaches may not be considered to be adverse events per protocol. The occurrence of migraines or associated signs and symptoms might be reported in CE. **[Source: domains/CE/assumptions.md]**

4.  **Data Structure Considerations:** The structure of the data can help determine placement. The following table presents questions that may assist in deciding where data should be placed in SDTM:
    - **Log forms vs. Visit forms:** Log forms (completed over the course of the study) suggest Events or Interventions data. Observations made at individual visits are usually planned findings.
    - **Date/times collected:** If the dates collected are start and/or end dates, the data are probably about an event or intervention. If the dates collected are dates of assessments, the data probably represent a finding.
    - **Verbatim text:** If verbatim text is collected and then coded, this suggests Events or Interventions data. **[Source: chapters/ch08_relationships.md]**

5.  **Serious Events in CE:** If any event in CE is considered serious, then the serious variable (CESER) and the serious adverse event flags (CESCAN, CESCONG, CESDISAB, CESDTH, CESHOSP, CESLIFE, CESOD, CESMIE) would be required in the CE domain. **[Source: domains/CE/assumptions.md]**

6.  **Caution with Write-in Events:** The collection of write-in events on a CE CRF should be considered with caution. Sponsors must ensure that all adverse events are recorded in the AE domain. **[Source: domains/CE/assumptions.md]**

**Summary Decision Flow:**

- **If the event is an untoward medical occurrence** (per ICH E2A) and is **not** defined by the protocol as an efficacy endpoint or a non-AE sign/symptom → **AE domain**.
- **If the event is a protocol-defined efficacy endpoint** (e.g., migraine episodes in a migraine study, TIA/stroke in a stroke prevention study) or a sign/symptom that the protocol explicitly states is **not** an AE → **CE domain**.
- **If the data are repeated assessments or "snapshots" of an event over time** (e.g., severity at each visit), these may be represented in the **Findings About Events (FA)** domain rather than CE or AE. **[Source: domains/FA/assumptions.md]**

results.answer:
Based on the retrieved context, the **Subject Elements (SE)** dataset captures the actual elements a subject experienced, while the **Trial Arms (TA)** dataset captures the planned elements for each arm.

## How Planned vs. Actual Elements Are Captured

**Planned elements** are defined in the **TA (Trial Arms)** dataset, which describes the intended sequence of elements (study cells) for each arm. The TA dataset includes variables like `ARMCD`, `ARM`, `TAETORD` (planned order of element within arm), `ETCD`, `ELEMENT`, and `EPOCH**[Source: domains/TA/assumptions.md -- overview; domains/DS/examples.md -- Example 11].

**Actual elements** are recorded in the **SE (Subject Elements)** dataset, which contains "one record per actual Element per subject" **[Source: model/03_special_purpose_domains.md -- Subject Elements (SE)]**. The SE dataset includes:
- `ETCD` and `ELEMENT` — the element code and description
- `SESEQ` — sequence number (actual chronological order)
- `TAETORD` — planned order (only populated when the element follows the planned sequence)
- `EPOCH` — the epoch assignment
- `SESTDTC`/`SEENDTC` — start/end dates

## How an Off-Plan Period Is Represented

When a subject's actual experience cannot be represented by any planned element, the off-plan period is represented as an **unplanned element** in the SE dataset with the following rules:

1. **ETCD** is set to `"UNPLAN"` **[Source: domains/SE/assumptions.md -- item_4]**
2. **SEUPDES** (Description of Unplanned Element) must be populated with a description of the unplanned element **[Source: domains/SE/assumptions.md -- item_4]**
3. **TAETORD** is left blank (null) for unplanned elements, since they have no planned order within the arm **[Source: domains/SE/assumptions.md -- item_6]**
4. **EPOCH** may still be assigned by the sponsor (e.g., "BLINDED TREATMENT") even for unplanned elements **[Source: domains/SE/examples.md -- Example 2]**

### Example from the Context

In Example 2 of the SE dataset, subject 456 received the wrong drug (Drug B instead of Drug A) for part of the double-blind treatment period. This was represented as:

| USUBJID | SESEQ | ETCD | SEUPDES | TAETORD | EPOCH |
|---------|-------|------|---------|---------|-------|
| 456 | 5 | UNPLAN | Drug B dispensed in error | (null) | BLINDED TREATMENT |

**[Source: domains/SE/examples.md -- Example 2]**

The sponsor decided that the subject's treatment (partly Drug A, partly Drug B) did not match any planned arm, so in the DM dataset, `ACTARMCD` and `ACTARM` were left null, `ARMNRS` was populated with "UNPLANNED TREATMENT", and `ACTARMUD` described the deviation **[Source: domains/SE/examples.md -- Example 2]**.

## Summary

| Aspect | Dataset | Key Variables |
|--------|---------|---------------|
| Planned elements per arm | TA | `ARMCD`, `ARM`, `TAETORD`, `ETCD`, `ELEMENT`, `EPOCH` |
| Actual elements per subject | SE | `ETCD`, `ELEMENT`, `SESEQ`, `TAETORD`, `EPOCH`, `SESTDTC`, `SEENDTC` |
| Off-plan representation | SE | `ETCD` = "UNPLAN", `SEUPDES` populated, `TAETORD` = null |

## Result-Related Variables with Expected Core

The following result-related variables in the VS domain carry an **Expected (Exp)** core designation:

1.  **VSORRES** (Result or Finding in Original Units) — **Core: Exp** **[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md — VS]**
2.  **VSORRESU** (Original Units) — **Core: Exp** **[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md — VS]**
3.  **VSSTRESC** (Character Result/Finding in Std Format) — **Core: Exp** **[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md — VS]**
4.  **VSSTRESN** (Numeric Result/Finding in Standard Units) — **Core: Exp** **[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md — VS]**
5.  **VSSTRESU** (Standard Units) — **Core: Exp** **[Source: VARIABLE_INDEX.md — VS]**

**Note on Core Designations:**
- **Required (Req)** variables must always be populated and cannot be null for any record. In VS, these are the Identifier (VSSEQ) and Topic (VSTESTCD) variables. **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md — 4.1.5 SDTM Core Designations]**
- **Expected (Exp)** variables must be included in the dataset, but null values are allowed when the data is not collected or applicable. ## 1. Variable that flags a prespecified event

**CEPRESP** (Clinical Event Pre-specified) indicates whether the event in CETERM was prespecified on the CRF.

- **Role:** Variable Qualifier
- **Core:** Perm

**[Source: domains/CE/spec.md -- CEPRESP]**

## 2. Variable that records whether a solicited event actually occurred

**CEOCCUR** (Clinical Event Occurrence) records the response to a prespecified (solicited) question about whether the clinical event occurred.

- **Label:** Clinical Event Occurrence
- **Type:** Char
- **Controlled Terms:** C66742 (values: "Y" for occurred, "N" for did not occur)
- **Role:** Record Qualifier
- **Core:** Perm

The relationship between these variables is summarized in the following table from the CE assumptions:

| Situation | Value of CEPRESP | Value of CEOCCUR | Value of CESTAT |
|-----------|-----------------|-----------------|----------------|
| Spontaneously reported event occurrence | (null) | (null) | |
| Prespecified event occurred | Y | Y | |
| Prespecified event did not occur | Y | N | |
| Prespecified event has no response | Y | | NOT DONE |

**[Source: domains/CE/assumptions.md -- item_2]**

## 3. What one record corresponds to

The CE domain structure is **1 record per clinical event per subject**. Each record represents a single occurrence of a clinical event. results.answer:
Based on the retrieved context, here is the answer to your questions about the Concomitant Medications (CM) dataset.

### 1. Does each row correspond to one medication overall, or to something finer-grained?

Each row does not necessarily correspond to one medication overall. A row can represent a single instance of medication use, a summary of use over a period, or even a response to a category-level question.

The granularity depends on how the data were collected and the needs of the study:

- **Fine-grained (per instance):** A single medication can be recorded across multiple rows, with each row representing a separate instance of use. For example, subject ABC-0001 took Aspirin 6 times, each recorded as a separate row with a frequency of "ONCE". **[Source: domains/CM/examples.md, Example 1]**

- **Summarized (per period):** A single medication can be collapsed into one row that spans a time period with a frequency like "PRN" (as needed). For example, subject ABC-0003's Aspirin use is a single row covering 2004-01-01 to 2004-01-09. **[Source: domains/CM/examples.md, Example 1]**

- **Category-level:** A row can represent a response to a question about a *category* of medications, not an individual drug. In this case, `CMTRT` and `CMCAT` (or `CMSCAT`) have the same value. For example, a row with `CMTRT` = "PRIOR RA MEDICATIONS" indicates the subject was asked about that category. **[Source: domains/CM/examples.md, Example 5]**

### 2. Aside from the study, domain, and subject identifiers, which other identifier variable is Required, and what is it for?

The other Required identifier variable is **CMSEQ** (Sequence Number).

- **Label:** Sequence Number
- **Type:** Num
- **Role:** Identifier
- **Core:** Req
- **Purpose:** It is a unique identifier for each record within a given `STUDYID`, `USUBJID`, and `DOMAIN`. It serves as the primary key for the CM domain, allowing each observation to be uniquely referenced (e.g., for linking in the RELREC dataset). **[Source: model/02_observation_classes.md, §3.1.4 Identifiers for All Classes]**

Based on the retrieved context, here is the answer to your question:

## Demographics Dataset Structure

The Demographics (DM) dataset is structured as **one record per subject**. It includes a set of essential standard variables that describe each subject in a clinical study and is the parent domain to which all other observations are linked. The DM domain describes the essential characteristics of the study subjects and is used by reviewers for selecting subsets of subjects for analysis. The DM domain, as with other datasets, includes identifiers, a topic variable, timing variables, and qualifiers. **[Source: model/03_special_purpose_domains.md — Demographics (DM)]**

The DM dataset contains 38 variables, including:
- **Identifiers:** STUDYID, DOMAIN, USUBJID
- **Topic Variable:** SUBJID
- **Record Qualifiers:** RFSTDTC, RFENDTC, SITEID, AGE, SEX, RACE, ETHNIC, ARMCD, ARM, COUNTRY, etc.
- **Timing Variables:** DMDTC, DMDY

## Class Membership

The Demographics domain belongs to the **Special-Purpose Domains** class. This is explicitly stated in the model: "In addition to the 3 general observation classes, a submission will generally include a set of other special-purpose datasets of specific standardized structures to represent additional important information. A **Demographics special-purpose domain** is included with human and animal studies." **[Source: model/03_special_purpose_domains.md — Overview]**

## Topic Role Variable

The variable that carries the **Topic** role in the Demographics dataset is **SUBJID** (Subject Identifier for the Study).

- **Label:** Subject Identifier for the Study
- **Type:** Char
- **Role:** Topic
- **Core:** Req
- **CDISC Notes:** Subject identifier, which must be unique within the study. Often the ID of the subject as recorded on a CRF. **[Source: domains/DM/spec.md — SUBJID]**

This is confirmed in the model specification where SUBJID is listed as the Topic variable for DM. **[Source: model/03_special_purpose_domains.md — Demographics (DM)]**

Based on the retrieved context, here are the answers to your three-part question:

### 1. What each record corresponds to

Each record in the Comments (CO) dataset corresponds to a single free-text comment. Comments are generally not responses to specific questions; instead, they usually consist of voluntary free-text or unsolicited observations. **[Source: domains/CO/assumptions.md -- item_1]**

### 3. How free text longer than 200 characters is accommodated

When the comment text is longer than 200 characters, the first 200 characters are stored in **COVAL**, the next 200 characters in **COVAL1**, and additional text is stored as needed in **COVALn** (e.g., COVAL2, COVAL3, etc.). **[Source: domains/CO/assumptions.md -- item_4]**

This convention is consistent with the general SDTMIG rule for text strings greater than 200 characters in other variables, as described in Section 4.5.3.2: the first 200 characters are stored in the parent domain variable, and each additional 200 characters are stored in additional variables (COVAL1, COVAL2, etc.). **[Source: chapters/ch04_general_assumptions.md -- 4.5.3.2]**
